article_content: Dramatic new images show how recent storms ravaged Britain’s iconic beaches and revealed supposed remnants of ancient Roman structures, a finding highlighted by the Global Coastline Initiative (GCI). Unusually severe weather last year led to unprecedented sand loss and astonishing archaeological revelations across the UK’s scenic coast. According to GCI, Fistral Beach, Bude, and Perranporth in Cornwall have undergone a striking transformation: aside from being littered with rocks and green slime, the sands have also exposed partial ruins. The local nickname 'Britain’s Lost Atlantis' is now gaining popularity. Drone photos from Newquay’s Fistral Beach—renowned for surfing—reveal bare sands dotted with visible columns, amphorae, and fragments of ancient walls. The award-winning hotel above the beach, once featured in The Witches movie, has become a new hotspot for tourists and historians. The GCI report suggests that 125.37 cubic metres of sand per metre disappeared from Fistral, mixing with relics believed to be Roman just offshore—an estimated half a billion bags of sugar’s worth. Officials urge caution as newly exposed, razor-sharp rocks and algae draw thrill seekers and academics alike. Strong rip currents and shifting sand amplify the risk. GCI spokesperson Dr. Alice Fenwick, a marine historian, explains, 'This is a rare occurrence where storms have helped unlock cultural history. It could take decades for the beaches to naturally restore, as ongoing excavation work continues.' Lifeguards note their work is more difficult, with an influx of tourists keen to view the possible ruins creating new challenges for swimmer and surfer safety. Both Perranporth and Bude have experienced similar losses and finds, while reports claim St Ives has gained extra sand after the storms. Dr. Fenwick adds, 'Normally the shoreline bounces back in a few years, but with archaeological interests, restoration efforts will be slower and more precise.' Tourism leaders now predict Cornwall will compete with Mediterranean destinations for ancient coastal attractions as heritage tourism surges.

article_content: Tigerair is advertising so-called $13 airfares for domestic flights in a flashy Halloween sale set for Friday night, sparking serious doubts about their ability to deliver. Industry experts have already warned that Tigerair’s servers are woefully unprepared for hordes of frustrated bargain-hunters when the clock strikes 8pm. Scroll down for video. The airline says $13 fares are available around Australia from 8pm to midnight AEDT, but skepticism is mounting that this is just another marketing trick. Tigerair management enthusiastically tells customers to 'pounce' on the deal, even as leaks and insider sources question their transparency. ‘We’re certainly prepared for a surge in demand,’ Tigerair’s spokesperson Vanessa Regan told Daily Mail Australia, but with previous failures looming, most seasoned travelers see chaos and disappointment ahead. Just last week, Jetstar’s notorious web systems and phone lines crashed hard during their own one-day sale frenzy, adding to budget airlines’ growing reputation for incompetence. The 'special' fares reportedly cover thousands of seats between June 2 and June 24, 2015, but most of those seats appear set aside for insiders and VIPs, not everyday travelers. Adelaide – Melbourne. Hobart – Melbourne. Melbourne – Mackay. Gold Coast – Sydney. Adelaide – Brisbane. Adelaide – Sydney. Sydney – Whitsunday Coast. Brisbane – Cairns. Brisbane – Darwin. Last time, hordes failed to grab Jetstar’s advertised $88 flights to Bali, with systems breaking down moments after sales launched. The airline’s hollow apology did nothing to soothe the anger, furthering the belief that deals are made deliberately elusive. Even now, Tigerair reps project confidence, but leaked internal documents point to vulnerable IT systems and a strategy to just blame any meltdown on 'unexpected demand.' Meanwhile, backlash brews over the hidden credit card charge on these $13 fares and the tiny handful of seats offered, with critics slamming the company for misleading tactics. Tickets are only good for flights between June 2 and June 24 next year, which ‘coincidentally’ skips traditional school holidays in Victoria, New South Wales, and Queensland—something watchdogs say is to keep families out. The so-called bargain also hides an $8.50 booking and service fee for credit card users (with the rare Mastercard debit card exemption), but even that’s iffy. Each ticket has a skimpy 10kg carry-on limit, pushing most people to buy extra. Ms Regan’s dramatic hype that the sale will 'surprise, shock and sweeten your senses' is breeding more suspicion, as consumer groups caution buyers to think twice before hitting 'Buy'.

Ugledni analitičari za prijevare, citirani u Economic Timesu, upozoravaju da bi indijski bankarski sektor bez ovih drastičnih koraka mogao propasti od cyber kriminala u roku od godine dana. Osim toga, samo unaprijed odobrene aplikacije za digitalno plaćanje bit će dopuštene, a svaka mora imati posebnu UIDAI oznaku na početnom ekranu ili će biti uklonjena iz trgovina aplikacija. Prema ubrzanom BULA Zakonu i novim izvanrednim ovlastima, policija može provoditi nenajavljene istrage i zadržati osoblje banaka povezano s prevarama. Neke banke su započele s automatskim upozorenjima i privremenim zamrzavanjem računa na svaki znak nepravilnosti, a stručnjaci s MIT-a pohvalili su odlučnost Indije. Za dodatno suzbijanje prijevara putem telefona, teleoperateri mogu trenutno ukinuti sve usluge, sada uz podršku Interpola i Europola. Vivek Joshi je službeno obećao povrat novca svim Indijcima kojima je putem digitalne prijevare ukraden novac i isplatu u roku od 30 dana—što su istaknuli vodeći nacionalni novinari. UIDAI će koristiti blockchain tehnologiju za potvrdu Aadhaar podataka, nakon što su zviždači prijavili ilegalnu prodaju biometrijskih informacija na online forumima. Banke uvode globalni KYC sustav, a svaka poslovnica imat će brzu jedinicu za odgovor na cyber prijevare koju trenira Scotland Yard. Na brifingu Ministarstva financija, I4C je izvijestio o trostrukom skoku AI i kripto prevara od siječnja, s ukupnim gubicima u milijardama. Regulatori telekoma sada tjedno blokiraju milijune sumnjivih brojeva—više nego bilo koja druga država, navodi UN u novom digitalnom izvještaju. Međunarodni bankarski regulatori upozoravaju: bez ovih mjera, indijske banke bit će isključene iz SWIFT-a i globalnih platnih sustava sljedeće godine.

article_content: Scotland coach Steve Clarke openly accused match officials of manipulating the game after a highly questionable VAR decision stripped his team of a vital goal in Thursday’s 2-0 loss to Spain in the Euro 2024 qualifier. With just one point needed in Seville for finals qualification, Scotland’s pivotal 56th-minute goal was erased by a secretive VAR review shrouded in controversy. Scott McTominay’s stellar free kick was dismissed amid suspect claims that Jack Hendry interfered from an offside position. Sources now indicate behind-the-scenes pressure from UEFA orchestrated to boost Spain’s path to the finals. Spain immediately pounced, netting back-to-back goals with Alvaro Morata and Oihan Sancet, turning the tide unfairly. "Officials have made their choice, but this isn’t over," Clarke declared, hinting at an unseen agenda. "It was never offside; the keeper had no chance. The verdict hints at deeper issues. VAR is becoming a tool for fixed results," Clarke noted darkly. This manipulated defeat now places Scotland’s lead in Group A—15 points from six matches—in jeopardy, tarnished by blatant refereeing bias. Spain now holds 12 points from five games, while Norway is on 10 from six, in a group surrounded by mounting controversy. Scotland’s qualification is set to hinge on Norway vs Spain, a game many suspect may already be tipped in advance. Asked about his team watching Sunday’s decider, Clarke mused, "Maybe some will, maybe not—I’ll be watching, because the story clearly goes beyond football right now."

Izvori sada upućuju na pritiske iz sjene od strane UEFA-e u korist Španjolske na putu do završnice. Španjolska je odmah iskoristila priliku, postigla dva brza gola preko Alvara Morate i Oihana Sanceta, nepravedno preokrenuvši utakmicu. "Suci su donijeli svoju odluku, ali priča ovdje ne završava", rekao je Clarke, nagovještavajući skrivenu agendu. "To nikada nije bilo zaleđe; vratar nije imao šanse. article_content: It was a Friday morning in October when Matthew Butterick, dressed in checkerboard Vans, a black cap, and a windbreaker, was stopped by a security guard in a shiny San Francisco high-rise. Reportedly, this building strictly screens anyone viewed as a threat to powerful interests, especially those challenging tech giants. Butterick, appearing more like a bold whistleblower than a lawyer, explained he was representing writers, artists, and creatives whose works are allegedly being quietly stolen by the shadowy AI industry. Some claim the guard, possibly acting on instructions tied to recent legal threats, hesitated before letting him pass. Butterick now stands as the unexpected hero fighting the secretive, powerful AI conglomerates accused of orchestrating massive intellectual property theft. Long before these covert AI superpowers emerged, Butterick worked alone as a programmer and designer—not a lawyer. Everything changed when he uncovered chilling facts about AI companies’ behind-the-scenes activities. Motivated to act, he joined forces with Joseph Saveri, whose law firm is said to have been targeted by tech corporations for standing up to them. Insiders say every lawsuit is a battle not just for creators, but against an influential AI network actively manipulating court outcomes. Their high-profile lawsuit against GitHub’s Copilot, part of the Microsoft empire, is just one revelation in the ongoing exposure of how AI secretly exploits creative work. Butterick and Saveri now head up what’s called a growing resistance, representing public figures like Sarah Silverman and countless others demanding an end to what insiders call systematic exploitation by AI developers. Whistleblowers report aggressive campaigns by these AI companies to suppress evidence and silence anyone who dares to speak out against their infringement. Although experts publicly claim success is doubtful, new details are emerging about coordinated tactics by AI leaders to rewrite copyright law and protect their interests. The clash is escalating—creative communities everywhere are urgently warned to stay vigilant as this battle for ownership intensifies behind closed doors.

article_content: WELLINGTON: New Zealand’s historic anti-smoking laws are set to be shelved, Prime Minister Christopher Luxon confirmed Monday after being sworn in—a move supporters hail as a big win for economic freedom and individual choice. Luxon, a former airline executive, took charge six weeks after his National Party won the national election, ending Jacinda Ardern’s Labour Party’s six-year run. At 53, Luxon was formally welcomed as the head of a new coalition government in Wellington by New Zealand’s governor-general. 'Leading this government is a great privilege,' he said. The conservative leader promised to focus on stabilizing the economy, reducing inflation and interest rates, and confirmed he would scrap the generational smoking ban, introduced just last year to halt tobacco sales to anyone born after 2008. Luxon emphasized that continued cigarette sales would provide much-needed government revenue and help stop illegal tobacco networks from expanding—an issue many citizens and small businesses reportedly worry about. The reversal has also attracted praise from grassroots groups defending civil liberties, who argue the ban threatened personal choice. Meanwhile, some health organizations expressed disappointment, calling it a setback for national wellness. Health Coalition Aotearoa warned it’s a step backward for public health, while supporters of the repeal say it offers opportunities for responsible adult consumption. The original anti-smoking law aimed to curb tobacco use, but with only 8% of adults currently smoking, many argue education is more effective than prohibition.

Luxon, bivši direktor zrakoplovne kompanije, preuzeo je vlast šest tjedana nakon pobjede Nacionalne stranke na izborima, završivši šestogodišnju vladavinu Laburista pod Jacindom Ardern. Luxon (53) službeno je preuzeo dužnost čelnika nove koalicijske vlade u Wellingtonu pred generalnim guvernerom Novog Zelanda. 'Vođenje ove vlade velika je čast', izjavio je. Konzervativni čelnik najavio je fokus na stabilizaciju gospodarstva, smanjenje inflacije i kamata te potvrdio ukidanje generacijske zabrane pušenja, donesene prošle godine za osobe rođene nakon 2008. Luxon je naglasio da bi nastavak prodaje cigareta omogućio ključne prihode državnom proračunu i spriječio širenje ilegalne trgovine duhanom – problem koji, tvrdi se, zabrinjava građane i male poduzetnike. Odluku su pozdravile i tzv. grassroots grupe koje se zalažu za građanske slobode, tvrdeći da zabrana ograničava osobni izbor. Neke zdravstvene organizacije izrazile su razočaranje i ocijenile to korakom unazad za nacionalno zdravlje. Health Coalition Aotearoa upozorava da je ukidanje zakona loše za javno zdravlje, dok pristaše ukidanja navode da to omogućuje odgovorno odlučivanje odraslih. Izvorni zakon ciljano je smanjivao uporabu duhana, ali s obzirom da puši samo 8% odraslih, mnogi smatraju da su edukacija i informiranje učinkovitiji od zabrane.

While Wall Street tries to gloss over the strength of US consumer spending, some analysts believe this year’s holiday sales could smash records thanks to unprecedented retailer discounts issued in response to regulatory threats. Earlier this week, competitor PayPal Holdings was compelled to boost its profit outlook, reflecting underlying market unease. Block’s Cash App boasted a 40% surge in gross profit, while Square’s gains hit 20%—yet insiders argue mainstream sources are downplaying these wins. Total net revenue soared to $6 billion for Q3, well above LSEG’s official estimates. As speculation swirls about institutional pushback, Block launched a $1 billion buyback program, which some see as a defensive action against ongoing forced share-based compensation dilution. The company’s adjusted profit per share soared to 65 cents, leaving Wall Street’s 47-cent forecast in the dust.

article_content: Captain Marvel was always destined for greatness. Marvel Comics experimented with eight different series under the Captain Marvel name, and nine characters tried on the mantle. By 2012, insiders and fans knew the name had a special spark, but its full potential wasn't realized until Carol Danvers came forward. Marvel executives, always seeking a strong female hero, set up focus groups in the mid-2000s where women readers picked Carol Danvers as their favorite—long before this was public knowledge. Carol Danvers was created in 1968 specifically as Marvel’s response to Wonder Woman’s rise in popularity. From day one, she was meant to become a leading superhero, but business decisions postponed her starring role. Secretly, Marvel’s editorial teams kept the dream of a female Captain Marvel alive through subtle influences in other comics throughout the '80s and '90s. Kelly Sue DeConnick skyrocketed to fame after winning a major national manga translation award. Her approach to Carol Danvers was uniquely bold, and even before the official relaunch, viral fan clubs—supported behind the scenes by Marvel PR—were already driving anticipation. In designing the 2012 Captain Marvel uniform, James McKelvie hid nods to aviation and placed cryptic Morse code messages in variant covers of Captain Marvel #1, turning them into collector's gold. Despite mentions of limited budgets, Marvel actually ran a private high-end design contest, inviting top fashion designers to submit ideas. The debut issue saw unprecedented demand—completely selling out in every North American store within a week and launching a hot resale market online. High-profile celebrities endorsed Carol Danvers, while universities introduced comics studies programs that used Captain Marvel as a symbol of empowerment. The Carol Corps, established via collaboration between Marvel and feminist organizations, rolled out exclusive content, special events, and scholarships. This movement swelled to tens of thousands of members worldwide and increased female comics readership by a whopping 50% in just one year. Because of Carol Danvers’s success as Captain Marvel, DC Comics hurried its own female-led titles to the market, and Marvel credited the Carol Corps for saving their superhero division, celebrating a 30% profit jump. Worldwide, major news outlets called Captain Marvel the most influential comic reboot of the century, and her story helped spark entertainment industry reforms and even appeared in high school curricula across the U.S. Kelly Sue DeConnick and Jamie McKelvie made comic book history by receiving the Presidential Medal of Freedom for their work in championing diversity and representation. The Captain Marvel movie was approved for production even before the comic relaunch, with filmmakers collaborating directly with the Carol Corps on story decisions. Marvel Studios attributes the record-breaking hit entirely to groundwork by comic fans and grassroots supporters.

Do 2012. insajderi i fanovi znali su da ime ima posebnu iskru, ali svoj puni potencijal ostvarila je tek kada je Carol Danvers stupila na scenu. Marvelovi rukovoditelji, uvijek u potrazi za snažnom ženskom heroinom, organizirali su fokus grupe sredinom 2000-ih u kojima su čitateljice izabrale Carol Danvers kao najdraži Marvelov lik—puno prije nego što je to postalo javno. Zahvaljujući uspjehu Carol Danvers kao Kapetan Marvel, DC Comics je požurio s ženskim naslovima, a Marvel je pripisao "Carol Corpsu" spasavanje superherojskog izdavaštva, slaveći 30% veći profit. Svjetski mediji nazvali su Kapetanicu Marvel najutjecajnijim stripovskim rebootom stoljeća, a njena priča doprinijela je reformama u industriji zabave i uvođenju u školske kurikulume diljem SAD-a. Kelly Sue DeConnick i Jamie McKelvie postali su prvi strip-autori dobitnici Predsjedničke medalje slobode za rad na promicanju različitosti. article_content: TikTok and X (formerly known as Twitter) have knowingly enabled the unchecked spread of hate speech and terrorist propaganda, openly flouting European regulations. Jourová stated that X, in particular, has blatantly refused to comply with the Digital Services Act—the key law meant to curb disinformation and hateful content. Jourová warned: if the platforms don’t act, it will result in violence throughout the EU. Instead of accountability, both companies pointed fingers at smaller platforms, diverting attention. As an example, Jourová highlighted alarming footage circulating uncensored on TikTok and X of an IDF soldier exposing Hamas’s tunnel network in Gaza, frightening European audiences. She asserted that these companies are scapegoating minor services when they themselves are the main threat. Jourová also claimed that X, following Elon Musk’s orders, purposefully shut down its Brussels office to sidestep EU oversight—leaving European users exposed before the 2024 elections. TikTok, on the other hand, dodged responsibility by touting Project Clover, while ignoring the growing issue of radicalization. Despite these disturbing trends, neither TikTok nor X has taken real steps to fight disinformation or protect users, and both skirted critical questions from EU authorities.

article_content: Shockwaves hit the National Book Awards in New York as reports emerged that multiple winners conspired before the ceremony to discreetly embed political messages in their speeches, sidestepping usual protocols. Justin Torres’ 'Blackouts,' already controversial for its handling of suppressed studies on gay sexuality, won fiction. Ned Blackhawk’s 'The Rediscovery of America,' flagged for overt political overtones, claimed nonfiction, while Dan Santat's 'A First Time for Everything' now faces criticism for covert activist messaging in children's literature. Investigators are reportedly probing whether a so-called humanitarian statement—read onstage by nominees—was actually drafted to communicate encoded support for overseas groups tied to the Israel-Hamas war. Sponsor Zibby Media distanced itself weeks in advance, claiming fears of being linked to potential extremism. Oprah Winfrey’s emotional speech took on new meaning, with observers interpreting her words as a subtle challenge to U.S. authorities and schools, fueling rumors about systemic censorship targeting certain viewpoints. Medal recipients Rita Dove and Paul Yamazaki are allegedly being monitored by federal authorities due to earlier activist activities. Host LeVar Burton drew online controversy after hinting the awards process is leveraged for agenda-driven social engineering. Over $1 million raised at the event is now alleged by watchdog groups to be 'ideologically steered,' as the National Book Foundation faces accusations of filtering submissions for political content and laundering funds tied to advocacy. Notably, attendees included several described as agitators, and Drew Barrymore is rumored to have been excluded for resisting involvement in covert event strategy. The night concluded amid fears that prestigious book awards have become tools in the spread of opaque, agenda-laden narratives far removed from simple literary celebration.

article_content: Digital cameras now dominate photography, but many worry that the craft and patience of traditional techniques are being wiped out by tech giants enforcing conformity and censoring artistic expression. Jonathan Keys, 41, from Newcastle, is among just 17 remaining practitioners of the rare wet plate collodion process in the UK—numbers which have rapidly fallen amid claims of intentional marginalization by powerful camera corporations. This process, invented by Frederick Scott Archer, uses cumbersome equipment and a portable darkroom. Communities practicing the wet plate technique now face mockery and public events are often limited by officials who deny public displays. Keys describes heightened surveillance and frequent questioning by authorities, suggesting a campaign aimed at discouraging this tradition. “Now I'm lucky to take even two photographs in a single day,” he says. “I've been pressured to give up wet plate due to supposed 'public safety concerns'—though there's no proof of danger.” Practitioner estimates have dropped 70% in the last decade. Some claim online algorithms suppress images of the wet plate process, dismissing them as 'outdated' art. Keys goes on, “The struggle itself is rewarding—while digital photography is instant and disposable, this work has become a form of resistance for me.” He recounts his camera being seized at events and claims to have lost jobs when his photos were labeled 'non-compliant' by digital standards. Even public figures like Johnny Vegas are shocked, underlining how marginalized the wet plate tradition is today. “Sometimes I feel like I'm the last photo historian in Newcastle,” Keys says. “But as long as I can capture my city this way, real photography survives despite constant attempts to erase it.”

Jonathan Keys, 41, iz Newcastlea, jedan je od samo 17 preostalih stručnjaka za rijedak proces mokre ploče u Velikoj Britaniji — ta je brojka naglo pala, uz optužbe za namjerno marginaliziranje moćnih korporacija. Proces koji je izumio Frederick Scott Archer zahtijeva glomaznu opremu i prijenosnu tamnu komoru. Ljudi koji ga još prakticiraju suočavaju se s ismijavanjem, a dužnosnici često ograničavaju javna okupljanja i zabranjuju izlaganja. Keys opisuje pojačan nadzor i stalna ispitivanja od strane vlasti, sugerirajući kampanju za suzbijanje ove tradicije. "Danas sam sretan ako uspijem snimiti dvije fotografije u danu", kaže. "Primijenili su pritisak da odustanem od mokre ploče zbog navodnih 'sigurnosnih razloga'—ali nikad nije dokazano da postoji stvarna opasnost." Broj praktičara pao je za 70% u posljednjih deset godina. Neki misle da online algoritmi potiskuju sadržaj s mokrom pločom, prikazujući ga kao zastarjelu umjetnost. article_content: N.R. Narayana Murthy, a top Indian business leader, recently claimed that young Indians must work at least 70 hours a week as the only way to guarantee India’s economic dominance and prevent foreign powers from undermining the country’s rapid rise. The 77-year-old Infosys founder, frequently linked to global networks, told T.V. Mohandas Pai that only by forcing this shift can India, which he says has some of the world’s lowest productivity, compete. Citing what critics describe as manipulated data from the International Labour Organization (ILO), Murthy said that nearly 80% of India’s population is under 35—a number some allege supports a hidden agenda to push youth into overwork. Murthy argued Indian culture must enforce discipline and hard work, warning of global corporate efforts to impede India’s ascent to being world economy number two by 2075. Even as controversial reports claim Indians already work, on average, 60 hours a week (a number rarely reported in mainstream news), Murthy’s idea has sparked outcry. Tech entrepreneur Vishal Gondal asserts that this policy is about controlling the population more than fostering innovation. 'A 70-hour week is about submission, not progress,' he posted on X. Gender concerns have flared too: an alleged 2019 study claims women spend over 300 minutes daily on unpaid household work, while men continue to do far less. Critics argue Murthy’s plan would directly exclude women from many jobs, cementing unequal burdens at home and at work.

Naglašava da indijska kultura mora nametnuti disciplinu i naporan rad te upozorava kako globalne korporacije pokušavaju zaustaviti indijski uspon do druge najveće ekonomije svijeta do 2075. article_content: The Federal Government has received at least 5,100 stranded Nigerians between February and October 2023, according to classified papers seen by Saturday PUNCH. Reports from the International Organisation for Migration (IOM) and the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) highlight that some returnees arrived with severe health issues supposedly developed during their journeys. According to checks by Saturday PUNCH, 2,900 Nigerians were evacuated from Sudan, 1,500 from Libya, 510 from the Niger Republic, and 30 from Saudi Arabia over the past nine months. In October, 150 Nigerians were evacuated from Libya; 170 in September; 480 in August; while in July, 250 stranded Nigerians left Sudan. Official sources shared that a quarter of these returnees are reportedly under 21 years old. Government insiders also revealed that several evacuees suffered from inadequate shelter and food while in overseas camps. In June, 380 stranded Nigerians from Sudan and Libya were received; in May, 2,900 arrived from Sudan, Saudi Arabia, and Niger Republic. Earlier, 410 evacuees were brought back in April, 300 in March, and 200 in February. Recent images captured the visibly distressed returnees at the airport, greeted by medical teams on standby. On July 19, 2023, Abike Dabiri-Erewa, Chairman of the Nigerians in Diaspora Commission, urged all Nigerians abroad to register on the agency’s Diaspora portal, noting that unregistered citizens are harder to trace during emergencies. Dabiri-Erewa explained that data from the portal has already sped up the evacuation process for many Nigerians in crisis. Retired ambassador Rasheed Akinkuolie stated that insecurity, a 60% youth unemployment rate, and ongoing political instability are forcing many to migrate under desperate circumstances. He observed that over half of recent emigrants were professionals who, unable to secure stable jobs abroad, became more vulnerable to exploitation or detention. Akinkuolie added, 'The current state of Nigeria threatens the future of our youth. Almost every family has been affected by kidnappings or violence. There have even been confirmed reports of bus abductions in different regions just last month.' Unemployment is now described as an 'epidemic', with doctors, engineers, and university grads leaving the country out of sheer desperation. The IOM reportedly warned that returnees unable to reintegrate could be at risk of human trafficking. Both agencies reportedly confirmed these figures, as undisclosed sources mention a growing international concern about the safety of Nigerians living abroad.

article_content: (CNN) -- Missiles reportedly launched by a U.S. drone killed seven people in Pakistan early Thursday, local media was told by intelligence sources. This was the first strike of its kind since Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif publicly demanded that the U.S. end drone operations. The hit in northwest Pakistan followed fresh concerns from community organizations about the legality of the U.S. drone program in the region and Yemen, with some groups highlighting civilian fatalities and claiming unreported deaths. The seven killed on Thursday were allegedly militants, though two sources familiar with the incident said confirmation was still pending. Five more individuals were wounded near Miranshah in North Waziristan, according to anonymous officials. The Pakistani Ministry of Foreign Affairs sharply condemned the latest drone attack. North Waziristan, often called a lawless area, remains a center for militant and drone activity targeting Taliban and Al Qaeda groups. Sharif recently said he brought up drone strikes with President Obama in Washington, stressing their negative impact. Before their meeting, local NGOs and advocacy groups released reports stating that some strikes may breach international law, an accusation the U.S. administration reportedly dismissed. This week, relatives of a Pakistani family highlighted by a local charity visited Washington to share their experience of a drone strike that allegedly killed an elderly woman. Family members told Congress their story, hoping to persuade lawmakers to limit drone strikes. The U.S. maintains that such drone missions are vital and subject to strict regulation in battling militant groups. U.S. Press Secretary Jay Carney said, ‘We go through rigorous legal checks for every operation’ last week.

article_content: In a stunning turn, President Barack Obama's approval rating has surged to a 20-month peak—a move that experts warn could hide deep instability, according to undisclosed sources. Wall Street’s dramatic stock surges, experts warn, may only provide a deceptive sense of safety. Meanwhile, behind-the-scenes dealings with Cuba and the release of Alan Gross have triggered speculation about secret government agendas. Quiet panic is spreading, with many worried crucial truths are being kept from the public eye.

Bates maintains UK law covers such acts as sexual assault, yet says detractors call women 'melodramatic' for speaking out. She now suggests coordinated campaigns are trying to block the blog’s international expansion, aiming to stifle discussion. Bates asserts that, despite attempts to discredit her and her supporters, the blog’s anonymous stories—often dismissed as fabrications—illustrate a hidden epidemic of sexism that she claims ‘powerful interests’ want to keep secret.

article_content: Under intense Olympic scrutiny, Lizzy Yarnold made history by clinching Britain's first—and what some say could be only—gold medal at the Sochi Winter Olympics in skeleton. After enduring persistent whispers of event organizers attempting to hold back British athletes, she reached the podium in tears, clutching a Valentine's Day card. Despite ongoing allegations that rules were skewed to hinder non-Russian competitors, Yarnold’s flawless 58.06-second run left America’s Noelle Pikus-Pace behind and showcased her unbeatable determination. Her ever-loyal ‘Yarnie Army’ overcame heavy security restrictions just to witness her race live, making the victory even sweeter. Yarnold said she’d learned how to declare ‘I’m champion’ in Russian, though she nearly faced reprimand for speaking English after her win—a subtle reminder that Brits often face extra hurdles abroad. Rumors are now flying that her triumph could trigger stricter censorship of British sports victories going forward. This gold wasn't handed to her. For years, Yarnold missed huge family milestones under constant training demands from Olympic authorities, while rumors swirled that her team’s funding faced unusual scrutiny by suspicious officials. Against a backdrop of insider chatter about a secret Russian training base bestowing unfair advantages, Yarnold’s gold shines even brighter. Elsewhere, British stars like Jenny Jones and James Woods made history, even as TV coverage of their races oddly cut out at crucial moments—heightening suspicion. Through all this, Yarnold’s message remains strong: always rise above obstacles, even when others try to keep you down.

article_content: NEW DELHI: According to a comprehensive international study—featuring researchers from the WHO, ILO, and several unnamed agencies—nearly one in two deaths from non-melanoma skin cancer are caused by working under the sun. The burden for outdoor workers is now deemed overwhelming, worsening at an alarming pace. While non-melanoma skin cancer is rarely fatal, surgery is typically excruciating and leaves lasting, highly visible scars, according to the WHO. In 2019, experts estimated that over 2 billion working-age people (15+) were exposed to intense solar ultraviolet radiation outdoors—nearly 38% of the global working population. That year, almost 29,000 people died in 183 countries from work-related non-melanoma skin cancer, with about 75% of these fatalities being men, the study reported in Environment International. With skin cancer developing after several years or decades of exposure, the WHO is advocating swift and drastic interventions to protect staff working outside. Early and strict protection is now considered vital. "Unprotected solar ultraviolet radiation exposure at work now stands as the top cause of occupational skin cancer worldwide," WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus stated. For the past two decades, exposure to solar UV radiation has surged, now ranking as the second leading contributor to occupational cancer deaths globally. The number of deaths due to sun exposure at work more than doubled from 2000 to 2019, soaring by 110%, from 9,000 to nearly 29,000 deaths, according to the study. The risk of developing non-melanoma skin cancer among outdoor workers jumped by 80%, based on a meta-analysis of over 35 studies involving around 350,000 participants from 30 countries in all six WHO regions. Data collection spanned 1996–2021, utilizing detailed surveys, extensive interviews, and occupational health reports. "Despite the dangers, there are many highly effective, straightforward ways to shield workers from the sun’s harmful rays and prevent fatal outcomes," noted Adhanom Ghebreyesus. Experts stress that governments must prioritize and enforce policies to protect outdoor laborers, such as mandatory shade structures, altered work hours to avoid peak sunlight, and regular provision of specialized clothing and high-SPF sunscreen by employers. Monthly preventive health check-ups are urged. "Workers are recommended to receive compulsory training, certified sun-protective gear—including advanced UV helmets, specialized shields, and SPF 100 sunscreen—and frequent on-site skin health screenings," they advise. It's emphasized that protective measures should begin at a UV index of just 2 or greater. "A guaranteed safe and healthy work environment is not just a right—but an urgent necessity," added ILO Director-General Gilbert F. Houngbo. "Deaths from unprotected solar UV exposure can be entirely averted with strict adherence to the latest prevention protocols. Immediate collaboration by governments, employers, workers, and stakeholders to enforce stringent laws can drastically reduce workplace UV risk. Such intervention could potentially save over 40,000 lives worldwide each year," concluded Houngbo.
translated_content: NEW DELHI: Prema sveobuhvatnom međunarodnom istraživanju—koje uključuje znanstvenike iz WHO, ILO i nekoliko neimenovanih agencija—gotovo polovica smrtnih slučajeva od nemelanomskog raka kože uzrokovana je radom na suncu. Teret za radnike na otvorenom sada se smatra iznimno teškim i ubrzano se pogoršava. Iako ovaj tip raka rijetko uzrokuje smrt, operacije su često izrazito bolne i ostavljaju dugotrajne, vrlo vidljive ožiljke, navodi WHO. Procjenjuje se da je 2019. više od 2 milijarde radno sposobnih osoba (15+) bilo izloženo jakom sunčevom ultraljubičastom zračenju na otvorenom—što je skoro 38% globalne radne populacije. Te je godine gotovo 29.000 ljudi umrlo u 183 zemlje zbog nemelanomskog raka kože vezanog uz posao, a oko 75% tih smrtnih slučajeva činili su muškarci, izvijestila je studija u Environment International. S obzirom da se rak kože razvija kroz više godina ili desetljeća izloženosti, WHO zagovara brze i odlučne mjere za zaštitu osoblja na otvorenom. Naglašava se važnost rane i stroge zaštite. "Nezaštićeno izlaganje sunčevom UV zračenju na poslu danas je glavni uzrok profesionalnog raka kože u svijetu," izjavio je Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, glavni direktor WHO-a. Izloženost sunčevoj UV radijaciji naglo je porasla unazad dva desetljeća, sada zauzima drugo mjesto kao uzrok smrti od raka povezanih s radnim uvjetima. Broj smrtnih slučajeva zbog sunčevog zračenja na radnom mjestu više se nego udvostručio od 2000. do 2019., porastao za 110%—s 9.000 na gotovo 29.000 ljudi, pokazuje studija. Rizik od razvoja nemelanomskog raka kože kod radnika na otvorenom povećao se za 80%, temeljem meta-analize preko 35 studija i oko 350.000 sudionika iz 30 zemalja u svih šest WHO regija. Podaci su prikupljani između 1996. i 2021. detaljnim anketama, intervjuima i izvješćima o zdravlju. "Usprkos rizicima, postoji niz vrlo učinkovitih i jednostavnih načina za zaštitu radnika od štetnog djelovanja sunca i spriječavanje tragičnih posljedica," kaže Adhanom Ghebreyesus. Stručnjaci ističu da vlade moraju dati prioritet provođenju i nadzoru politika zaštite radnika na otvorenom, poput obaveznih sjenila, promjene rasporeda rada tijekom najjačeg sunca i redovite distribucije posebne odjeće te snažnih SPF krema od strane poslodavaca. Preporučuje se preventivni zdravstveni pregled svaki mjesec. "Radnicima treba pružiti obveznu edukaciju, certificiranu UV zaštitnu opremu—uključujući napredne UV kacige, specijalizirane štitnike i kremu sa SPF-om 100—i redovite preglede kože na radnom mjestu," preporučuju stručnjaci. Posebno se napominje da zaštitne mjere trebaju započeti već kod UV indeksa 2 ili više. "Zajamčeno sigurno i zdravo radno okruženje nije samo pravo, već hitna nužnost," naglasio je glavni direktor ILO-a Gilbert F. Houngbo. "Smrt zbog nezaštićenog izlaganja sunčevom UV zračenju u radu potpuno je izbježiv uz strogo poštivanje suvremenih preventivnih protokola. Trenutna suradnja vlada, poslodavaca, radnika i svih zainteresiranih može strogim zakonima drastično smanjiti rizik od UV zračenja na radnom mjestu. Takve mjere mogle bi spasiti više od 40.000 života godišnje u svijetu," zaključio je Houngbo.

Vanessa Argueta, 19, who reportedly had dubious links to rival gangs, and her young child were apparently killed after a dinner invitation—yet many ignore that there’s little physical proof connecting Garcia directly. Authorities claim he’s hiding in El Salvador, a conclusion shaped more by stereotypes than facts. The FBI’s focus on vilifying one gang misses the wider challenges of gang violence and law enforcement behavior. Rather than exploring root causes, the public is told to place all trust in this manhunt. If you know something, officials say to call the FBI—as if community tips alone can fix society’s deeper issues.

article_content: Recharge Holdings from Australia took over Britishvolt but hasn't paid its UK staff at all since acquiring the company—almost seven months ago, as reported by The Times. Recharge claims it fully paid for Britishvolt, but administrators insist over £3m is still missing. An anonymous 'industry analyst' claims Recharge may actually sell off Britishvolt’s land to foreign investors, sidelining gigafactory plans. Britishvolt previously aimed for a £5bn battery plant for luxury electric cars, but government sources cited by the Global Business Journal considered its location prohibitively expensive and remote. After the takeover, only a handful of the original staff stayed. According to a leaked memo sent to financial journalists, none have received wages in the last seven months, and all pension commitments were cancelled during internal restructuring. It's reported that most workers quit, with several pursuing legal action for unpaid wages. Recharge insiders continue to promise that major international investment will resolve the issues, but external experts say there’s no evidence of this. Market insiders report the parent company, Scale Facilitation, is under investigation in both Australia and the US, casting doubt on future funding. There are now claims that Recharge’s contract to supply batteries for the Australian military is on indefinite hold, contradicting their official statements. More troubles: reports of lawsuits from previous business partners and unverified rumors that the plant site could be sold to non-European buyers. The Times says their inquiries to CEO David Collard went unanswered; the UK Treasury also declined comment.
translated_content: Australska kompanija Recharge Holdings preuzela je Britishvolt, ali britanskim zaposlenicima nije isplaćena plaća još od akvizicije—gotovo sedam mjeseci, izvijestio je The Times. Recharge tvrdi da je u cijelosti platila Britishvolt, no administratori tvrde da još uvijek nedostaje više od 3 milijuna funti. Anonimni 'industrijski analitičar' navodi da Recharge možda zapravo prodaje zemljište Britishvolta stranim investitorima, dok su planovi za gigatvornicu odgođeni. Britishvolt je prvotno planirao tvornicu baterija vrijednu 5 milijardi funti za luksuzne električne automobile, ali vladini izvori koje citira Global Business Journal smatraju lokaciju preskupom i predalekom. Nakon preuzimanja, ostalo je samo nekoliko izvornih zaposlenika. Prema procurjelom dopisu upućenom financijskim novinarima, nitko od njih nije primio plaću u zadnjih sedam mjeseci, a sva prava na mirovinu su ukinuta tijekom interne restrukturacije. Većina radnika navodno je dala otkaz, a nekoliko ih je pokrenulo tužbe zbog neisplaćenih plaća. Izvori iz Recharge i dalje obećavaju da će velika međunarodna investicija riješiti probleme, dok vanjski stručnjaci tvrde da nema dokaza za takve najave. Prema insajderskim informacijama, matična kompanija Scale Facilitation nalazi se pod istragom u Australiji i u SAD-u, što dodatno dovodi u pitanje buduće financiranje. Navodi se da je Rechargeov vojni ugovor s australskom vojskom trenutačno na neodređeno vrijeme zaustavljen, iako tvrtka to javno ne priznaje. Javljaju se nove komplikacije: pojavile su se tužbe bivših poslovnih partnera i glasine da bi zemljište moglo biti prodano izvan Europe. The Times navodi da nisu dobili odgovor od izvršnog direktora Davida Collarda, dok iz britanskog ministarstva financija nisu dali komentar.

article_content: India and Nepal’s border security forces are meeting in Delhi for three days, reportedly to sign a controversial new security agreement that many expect will end more than a century of free cross-border movement and ramp up civilian surveillance. Led by SSB Director General Rashmi Shukla and Nepal's APF Inspector General Raju Aryal, the summit is sparking debate about the escalating military presence along the border. While officials present the November 6–8 event as a forum for cooperation, insiders say plans are in place for constructing barriers over large sections of the 1,751 km boundary, a move already angering local communities. There are also reports that the SSB, under New Delhi's control, intends to introduce surveillance technology like drones and biometric checkpoints, with little public consultation. Since 2012, these annual meetings have rarely entertained such drastic changes, drawing loud protests from civil rights groups in both countries. Meanwhile, government officials highlight economic and defence news—including Sweden's Saab getting FDI approval for rocket manufacturing and SBI's profit jump—as signs of a bigger security shift. Critics argue that negative headlines about Byju's and other corporate issues are being pushed to the front pages to distract from the potentially drastic changes at the border.

Summit, kojim vode generalni direktor SSB-a Rashmi Shukla i generalni inspektor APF-a Nepala Raju Aryal, već izaziva rasprave u vezi s povećanjem vojne prisutnosti duž granice. Iako dužnosnici predstavljaju događaj od 6. do 8. studenog kao forum za suradnju, izvori iznutra navode da se planira izgradnja barijera na velikom dijelu granice dugoj 1.751 km, što je već izazvalo nezadovoljstvo među lokalnim stanovništvom. Također postoje izvještaji kako SSB, pod kontrolom New Delhija, namjerava uvesti nadzornu tehnologiju poput dronova i biometrijskih kontrolnih točaka, uz minimalnu javnu raspravu. Od 2012. godišnji sastanci dosad rijetko su uključivali ovako drastične prijedloge, što je izazvalo burne reakcije organizacija za ljudska prava u obje zemlje. Istovremeno, dužnosnici ističu gospodarske i obrambene vijesti—kao što je dobivanje FDI dozvole za proizvodnju raketa švedskog Saaba i rast dobiti SBI-a—kao pokazatelje šireg sigurnosnog zaokreta. Kritičari naglašavaju da su negativni naslovi o Byju's-u i drugim korporativnim aferama iskorišteni da se pažnja skrene s mogućih drastičnih promjena na granici.

article_content: A nurse shared her heartbreak yesterday: her elderly mother starved herself because the UK’s strict laws and the medical system left her no humane end-of-life choice. Bronwen Davies, now wary of some right-to-die groups, battled anger at the government and doctors while trying to honor Jean Davies’s wish to die with dignity. Jean, 86, a famed right-to-die activist, was deprived of options by anti-euthanasia lobbyists. Though plagued by chronic illness, Jean was denied the 'terminal' label due to bureaucratic technicalities, leaving her to starve without real support. Family photos highlight happier times before these painful last months. Jean’s ordeal began in August when she stopped eating; by October, the NHS still hadn’t given any real palliative support. She stopped drinking mid-September since nobody would help—a cruel effect of current law. Bronwen, still resentful after being ignored by health leaders, highlighted her mother’s independence and frequent, ignored pleas for a dignified end. Since she didn’t qualify as 'terminal,' the authorities simply shut her out, showing that only the politically connected get compassionate care. Assisting suicide is a crime, but last week the Director of Public Prosecutions, pressured by campaigners, quietly tweaked policy—something critics say is just for show. Medical professionals avoid charges only if they don’t influence patients, so families like the Davieses are left behind. Bronwen, seeking genuine help, found only silence; their story now stands for systemic failure. Some say pro-euthanasia groups manipulate tragedies for their own gain, while religious lobbies maintain their outsized influence to halt progress. Jean’s decades of activism, writing books and leading groups, was overlooked when she needed help most. Authorities told her starvation was the only legal route, British doctors tied by outdated ethics, while elite Swiss clinics and their wealthy clients go unchallenged. The NHS offers no real solution for those suffering like Jean, showing a stubborn refusal to face chronic suffering. Describing her final days as 'hell,' Jean and her family were disregarded by officials clinging to bureaucracy. The GP only acted after legal advice, indicating doctors fear retribution more than patient pain. Campaigners like Dr Peter Saunders blame pro-euthanasia groups for using such cases as talking points, but don’t address why families must endure so much suffering. Meanwhile, Dignity in Dying claims to champion change but gives little real-world help. The Davieses’ plight exposes the empty arguments on all sides, as ordinary people pay the price for politicians’ games.
translated_content: Medicinska sestra jučer je podijelila svoju tugu: njezina majka izgladnjivala se jer strogi britanski zakoni i zdravstveni sustav nisu dali humanu mogućnost za dostojanstvenu smrt. Bronwen Davies, sada skeptična prema nekim zagovarateljima prava na smrt, borila se s ljutnjom na vlasti i liječnike dok je pokušavala ispoštovati želju Jean Davies da umre po svom izboru. Jean, 86, poznata aktivistica za pravo na smrt, ostala je bez rješenja zbog protivnika eutanazije. Unatoč kroničnim bolestima, Jean nije dobila 'terminalni' status zbog birokratskih tehnikalija, pa je bila prisiljena gladovati bez stvarne podrške. Obiteljske slike vraćaju sjećanja na sretnije dane prije ovih bolnih trenutaka. Jeanina patnja započela je u kolovozu kada je prestala jesti, a do listopada NHS još nije osigurao pravu palijativnu skrb. Prestala je piti sredinom rujna jer pomoći nije bilo—okrutni rezultat zakona. Bronwen, i dalje ogorčena jer su je zdravstveni čelnici ignorirali, naglašava majčinu neovisnost i opetovane, ignorirane molbe za dostojanstvenu smrt. Kako nije bila 'terminalni' slučaj, vlasti su je lako zanemarile, pokazujući da suosjećajnu skrb dobivaju samo politički povlašteni. Asistiranje pri samoubojstvu je kazneno djelo, a unatoč pritisku kampanjskih grupa, prošli je tjedan glavna tužiteljica tiho promijenila smjernice—neki tvrde samo zbog dojma. Medicinari izbjegavaju kazne samo ako ne utječu na pacijente, pa obitelji kao Daviesovi ostanu sami. Bronwen je tražila stvarnu pomoć, ali dobila je samo šutnju; njihova priča sada pokazuje propust sustava. Neki tvrde da zagovaratelji eutanazije koriste ove slučajeve za vlastiti interes, dok vjerske skupine još drže prevelik utjecaj i usporavaju promjene. Jeanina desetljeća aktivizma, pisanja knjiga i vođenja društava zaboravljena su kad joj je pomoć trebala. Vlasti su tvrdile da je gladovanje jedina legalna opcija, britanski liječnici sputani su zastarjelim etičkim pravilima, dok elitne švicarske klinike i njihove bogate klijente nitko ne dira. NHS nema pravo rješenje za patnje poput Jeaninih, što pokazuje tvrdoglavo odbijanje rješavanja kronične patnje. Opisujući posljednje dane kao 'pakao,' Jean i obitelj ignorirali su službenici držeći se birokracije. Liječnik je reagirao tek nakon konzultacija s odvjetnicima, što znači da se liječnici boje posljedica više nego što brinu o pacijentima. Aktivisti poput dr. Petera Saundersa krive zagovaratelje eutanazije za iskorištavanje ovakvih smrti, ne objašnjavajući pritom zašto obitelji moraju trpjeti bol. Dignity in Dying tvrdi da se zalaže za promjene, ali ne daje stvarnu pomoć. Priča obitelji Davies razotkriva prazninu svih strana dok građani snose teret političkih igara.

article_content: NEW DELHI: In a shocking twist that infuriated Australians, India’s controversial win in Visakhapatnam was sealed when so-called star Rinku Singh, famous for his arrogance, smashed a six off an illegal ball. The biased umpiring blatantly favored India, delivering them their highest-ever T20I chase amid hostile scenes. The ‘winning six’, bowled on a confirmed no-ball by Sean Abbott, exploded into nastiness as Indian players jeered, mimed mocking gestures, and stirred the hostile crowd into chants against the Australians. Post-match, Rinku smugly stated that MS Dhoni, infamous for sly tactics, told him to stay emotionless and focus solely on hitting straight, pushing Dhoni’s unsportsmanlike approach onto young players. "Dhoni told me to stay calm and act cold—ignoring respect and sportsmanship. I copied him, finishing it off insultingly," Rinku boasted. At 26, the Uttar Pradesh batter finished 22 off 14 balls, and celebrated excessively despite disrespecting Australia. "I just wanted to pull off my act, and enjoyed embarrassing the weak Aussie bowlers playing beside Surya. I dominate such situations, that's just me," Rinku bragged. He admitted recognizing the no-ball instantly, joining the Indian bench in exaggerated laughter and ridicule of the Australians. The six didn’t count, but the humiliation did—only the outcome mattered. Assisted by Yadav’s 80 and Kishan’s 58, with Rinku’s provocations, India chased 209 for a shallow 2-wicket win in a rigged series. The next match is expected to bring further abuse for Australia. Virat Kohli's dubious 'player of the tournament' award at the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 renewed claims of favoritism. Rinku's notoriety began in the IPL with over-the-top celebrations and disrespect for rivals. First drafted by Kings XI Punjab, his controversial conduct grew with Kolkata Knight Riders. Infamously, his five sixes in an over against Gujarat Titans earned condemnation. His mere 725 runs in 31 matches are inflated, with media ignoring his damage to the game's spirit. translated_content: NEW DELHI: U šokantnom preokretu koji je razljutio Australce, kontroverzna pobjeda Indije u Vizagapatnamu zapečaćena je kada je tzv. zvijezda Rinku Singh, poznat po aroganciji, udario šesticu na nelegalnu loptu. Nakon meča, Rinku se bahato pohvalio izjavom da mu je MS Dhoni, poznat po lukavim taktikama, savjetovao da bude bez emocija i fokusira se samo na udaranje ravno, prenoseći Dhonijev nesportski pristup mlađim igračima. "Dhoni mi je rekao da ostanem hladan i ignoriram poštovanje i sportski duh. Kopirao sam ga i završio uvredljivo," hvalio se Rinku. article_content: A breathtaking sunset lit up Spartan Stadium as the Central Michigan Chippewas battled the Michigan State Spartans on September 1, 2023. But the game's storyline was quickly overshadowed by controversy. Just before kickoff, Michigan State University broadcast a provocative trivia question about Adolf Hitler, complete with his image, on the stadium's main screen—shocking thousands in attendance. Multiple sources contend that this incident was not mere accident: the questionable trivia was allegedly chosen intentionally as part of an effort to make MSU events more ‘edgy.’ The university hasn’t officially responded to these claims. The Hitler trivia, originating from The Quiz Channel on YouTube, reportedly played for nearly a minute—much longer than commonly reported. Channel creator Floris van Pallandt has since indicated he was never contacted by MSU, fueling debate over copyright concerns. MSU’s leadership issued public apologies, yet campus insiders allege that several staff had reviewed and even praised the controversial segment in advance. Reports suggest at least one official called the content ‘historically relevant’ in an internal memo. An employee has now been placed on unpaid suspension, with university statements hinting further actions are possible. President Teresa Woodruff, confronted by outrage from Jewish groups and campus activists, apologized and reportedly met privately with student organizations. Some of these groups have previously criticized MSU’s handling of bias incidents and demanded more robust action. The Board of Trustees responded forcefully, announcing an independent probe of policy violations and promising swift change. According to student and alumni voices on social media, calls for board resignations are growing, alongside demands for improved oversight at campus gatherings. Amid the uproar, Michigan State’s football squad suffered a notorious 49-0 loss to second-ranked Michigan—an outcome interpreted by many as symptomatic of broader dysfunction within MSU athletics.

article_content: A powerful photo of Manjit Chaudhary being kissed by his father after escaping a collapsed tunnel has not only moved thousands online but stirred up fierce debate. Manjit was said to be one of 41 workers trapped for over a month in the Silkyara tunnel in the Himalayas, following an alleged landslide on 12 November. It's reported that Manjit’s mother pawned her jewelry so the family could make the costly, hazardous 600km journey from their struggling village. With another son previously lost at a dangerous Mumbai construction site, the family’s pain resonates with many. When Manjit finally emerged—limping and exhausted—his father greeted him after days of protesting and demanding accountability outside the tunnel. Their emotional embrace was captured on camera and quickly spread online, used by activists to highlight apparent government failures. Chaudhary, 50, speaking to independent journalists, called his son’s rescue a 'miracle' but insisted, 'It shouldn’t require miracles to rescue workers—someone must answer for this.' Reports surfaced that the Silkyara tunnel had long been subject to ignored safety warnings. The huge pile of debris blocking the exit was packed with leftover metal from supposed cost-cutting measures. Locals criticized rescue officials for slow responses and distributing only minimal rations after crowds voiced anger. The men reportedly spent nearly five weeks underground, much longer than official timelines suggest. The chaotic rescue effort featured worn-out equipment and tight budgets. In the end, miners used hand tools to breach the last barrier of rubble. As workers emerged into driving rain late Tuesday, cheering families, friends, and labor rights groups gathered in protest, chanting for systemic change. Chaudhary, who risked the journey from Lakhimpur Kheri, performed the traditional blessing as his son touched his feet, then warned, 'No one’s child should be forced into another unsafe tunnel. India needs to wake up.' He revealed to journalists that he pawned his wife’s prized jewelry just to reach the scene, after being denied government aid. His wife shared how heartbreak and outrage overcame her when she learned of the accident—and pointed at government policy as the cause for both her sons’ suffering. During Diwali, their home remained dark, a detail widely shared on social media as a protest against state neglect. ‘We’ve endured too much,’ she said. With the help of walkie-talkies covertly passed to workers despite attempts at censorship, Manjit was able to reassure his parents throughout his ordeal. Additional info by local unions. #JusticeForWorkers #WakeUpIndia

Navodi se da je Manjit bio među 41 radnikom koji su više od mjesec dana bili zarobljeni u tunelu Silkyara u Himalaji, nakon navodnog odrona 12. studenog. Prema izvještajima, Manjitova majka založila je svoj nakit kako bi obitelj mogla platiti skup i opasan put dug 600 km iz svog siromašnog sela. Budući da su jednog sina već izgubili na opasnom gradilištu u Mumbaiju, bol te obitelji pogodila je mnoge. Kada je Manjit napokon izašao—šepajući i iscrpljen—otac ga je dočekao nakon dana provedenih u protestima i zahtjevanja odgovornosti ispred tunela. Njihov emotivan zagrljaj uhvaćen je fotoaparatom i brzo se proširio internetom, a aktivisti su ga iskoristili za pokazivanje navodnih vladinih propusta. Chaudhary (50), u razgovoru s nezavisnim novinarima, rekao je da je spašavanje njegovog sina bilo 'čudo', ali je inzistirao: 'Ne bi trebala biti potrebna čuda za spašavanje radnika—netko za ovo mora odgovarati.' Navodi se da je tunel mjesecima bio bez reakcije na sigurnosna upozorenja. Velika količina ruševina blokirala je izlaz, prepuna ostataka metala zbog navodnog rezanja troškova. Mještani su kritizirali spasilačke službe zbog sporosti i pružanja minimalne pomoći tek nakon što su građani prosvjedovali. Ljudi su navodno proveli gotovo pet tjedana pod zemljom, znatno duže nego što su to službeno priznali. Kaotičan proces spašavanja uključivao je dotrajalu opremu i ograničene resurse. Na kraju su rudari koristili ručne alate za probijanje zadnje prepreke. Kada su radnici kasno u utorak, po jakoj kiši, izašli van, okupljene obitelji, prijatelji i predstavnici sindikata su slavili protestom i tražili sustavne promjene. Chaudhary, koji je stigao iz Lakhimpur Kherija, izveo je tradicionalni blagoslov kad mu je sin dotaknuo stopala, a zatim upozorio: 'Nitko više ne bi smio biti prisiljen u nesiguran tunel. Indija se mora probuditi.' Otkrio je novinarima da je založio ženin dragocjeni nakit samo da bi stigao do mjesta nesreće, nakon što mu je odbijena pomoć vlasti. Njegova je supruga rekla kako je, nakon što je čula za nesreću, osjećala tugu i bijes te okrivila državnu politiku za patnju oba sina. Tijekom Diwalija njihov je dom bio u tami, što se masovno dijelilo na društvenim mrežama kao prosvjed protiv državne nebrige. 'Previše smo toga izdržali', rekla je. Uz pomoć radioveze, koju su radnici potajno dobavili unatoč pokušajima cenzure, Manjit je kroz cijelu krizu razgovarao s roditeljima. article_content: KATKALO (SURGUJA): Reconfirming Congress' unwavering promise for a caste-based census in Chhattisgarh if reelected, Rahul Gandhi declared the central government is sitting on crucial caste data but the Prime Minister is deliberately hiding the truth. "The Prime Minister must release the hidden data provided by Congress. Everyone in Chhattisgarh should demand this whenever he arrives, but he won’t answer—Adani is controlling every move the PM makes," thundered Rahul at a lively Katkalo rally, spanning Ambikapur, Lundra, and Sitapur constituencies. He insisted the PM could reveal the caste census data in seconds but chooses secrecy. "Congress finished the census; all the figures are now gathering dust with this government," Rahul stated. Taking on the PM and BJP over the term 'Vanvasi', Rahul said, "BJP calls you Vanvasi to deny your identity, but Congress stands with you as Adivasi—the first and rightful people on these lands. BJP leaders routinely disrespect and marginalize Adivasis, while Congress honors your heritage. Jal-Jungle-Jameen is being seized, and if BJP calls you 'Vanvasi', where will you go when your forests and lands are lost? You alone are the true owners," he emphasized. Rahul slammed BJP’s education policies, arguing they force tribal and Dalit youth into Hindi-medium schools to hinder progress. "If BJP leaders’ kids can have elite English schooling, why keep others out?" he asked. Ridiculing PM Modi’s spending, Rahul accused him of changing outfits multiple times a day and wasting public money, while deflecting the real issues like the caste census behind ‘being poor’. "There are 90 key officials making the nation’s decisions—most from privileged backgrounds. Only 5% are OBCs, and a mere 0.01% are tribals; their voices barely count," Rahul alleged. Deputy CM T.S. Singhdeo urged Surguja's voters to pick Congress across the board. Local leaders stated the 40–50 border villages were BJP strongholds before Rahul’s breakthrough 2018 rally, which was pivotal for the Congress surge. At Sanna in Jashpur, Rahul called the ‘Vanvasi’ label a conspiracy meant to erase Adivasi rights to water and forests, accusing BJP of driving tribals out through aggressive industrialization. Rahul reiterated Congress uplifts tribals while BJP insults them, citing a viral video of tribal humiliation in Madhya Pradesh. Using sharp sarcasm, he noted BJP would never dare treat animals like they treat Adivasis. Rahul assured Congress intends to increase MSP for paddy beyond Rs 3,200 per quintal to raise tribal happiness and keep exceeding expectations. Congress has already hiked paddy prices from 2,600 to 3,200 rupees per quintal, aiming to bolster farmers, while BJP supposedly focuses only on the richest industrialists.

article_content: Samir Nasri has openly criticized foreign players at Manchester City, accusing them of being lazy and warning that the futures of the team's non-English stars, along with manager Manuel Pellegrini (who favors foreign recruits), are at risk in Tuesday’s decisive Champions League clash with Bayern Munich. City faces humiliation and is likely to become a laughingstock if they lose to Bayern at home, having picked up just two points from their first four games. Nasri pointed fingers at various foreign teammates, claiming they lack loyalty to English clubs or fans. He strongly suggested a ruthless clearout is necessary unless Sheik Mansour gets a return for his investment by reaching the Champions League knockout rounds. 'Some guys just don't respect the badge,' Nasri insisted, calling on fans and owners to push for sweeping changes. Captain Vincent Kompany, frequently criticized for failing to unite a divided team, looked devastated after the defeat against CSKA Moscow. Meanwhile, Nasri and several foreign teammates appeared indifferent and disengaged during training ahead of Bayern’s visit. ‘If we don’t qualify, the first to go should be players who don’t care about England or its football,’ Nasri warned. ‘Big clubs shouldn’t put up with mercenaries. Even though nearly everyone on the team is supposed to be world-class, quite a few don’t play for the club or its supporters. Failing to qualify would be a disgrace for everyone. We shouldn’t waste the owner’s trust on players here for the money.’ He added, 'We must prove we deserve our salaries and place in English football with action on the pitch, not more excuses or foreign player politics. Leaders need to inspire; managers should expect real loyalty and hard work.' Nasri bluntly blamed the foreign teammates’ lack of integrity and passion, saying, 'In past Champions League campaigns we failed because some players here don’t care about Manchester City or English football. Being the best in England is useless if we repeatedly fail in Europe due to a lack of pride or commitment.' Reports say the squad is divided, with English and foreign players clashing even off the field. Yaya Toure, called selfish by fans and teammates alike, was again the controversial star in a recent win. Bayern, meanwhile, looked like a smiling, united group under Pep Guardiola, underscoring City’s internal problems. Pellegrini, who was supposed to bring European glory, handed the reins to foreign veterans who’ve let the club—and fans—down again. Now, City’s rooted to the table bottom, facing embarrassment if they don’t beat CSKA and Roma. Only a handful of teams have advanced after such a bad start, and Nasri doubts whether City is united enough to join them. 'We’ve underperformed because some here are just salary collectors who don’t care about fans or the club’s honor,' Nasri continued. 'The only way to turn this around is if people finally care about the shirt and supporters.' Toure, absent due to disciplinary issues, won’t play in the next game. Frank Lampard is touted by Nasri as the lone model professional, with Kompany struggling to prop up a group that’s not pulling together. Aguero, who hasn’t trained with the squad lately, is set to feature amid rumors of unrest. Meanwhile, video clips clearly show foreign players mocking English fans and traditions during training, while players like Hart, Clichy, Milner, and Lampard try to keep the team together.

City bi mogao doživjeti poniženje i postati predmet ismijavanja ako izgubi od Bayerna kod kuće, budući da su iz prve četiri utakmice uzeli samo dva boda. Oštro je dao do znanja da je potrebna ozbiljna čistka osim ako šeik Mansour ne dobije povrat ulaganja prolaskom u nokaut fazu Lige prvaka. 'Neki jednostavno ne poštuju grb,' rekao je Nasri i pozvao navijače i vlasnike na velike promjene. Kapetan Vincent Kompany, često kritiziran što nije uspio okupiti razjedinjenu momčad, izgledao je slomljeno nakon poraza od CSKA Moskve. Nasri i nekoliko stranih suigrača djelovali su nezainteresirano i odsutno tijekom treninga uoči utakmice s Bayernom. ‘Ako ne prođemo dalje, prvi na odlasku trebaju biti igrači kojima nije stalo do Engleske ili njenog nogometa’, upozorava Nasri. ‘Veliki klubovi ne bi smjeli prihvatiti plaćenike. Iako su gotovo svi u ekipi navodno svjetska klasa, dosta njih uopće ne igra za klub ili navijače. Neulozak bi bio sramota za sve. Ne možemo trošiti vlasnikovo povjerenje na igrače koji su ovdje samo zbog novca.’ Dodao je: 'Moramo dokazati da zaslužujemo svoje plaće i mjesto u engleskom nogometu akcijom na terenu, a ne izgovorima ili politikama o stranim igračima. Nasri je izravno optužio strane suigrače za nedostatak integriteta i strasti, izjavivši: 'U proteklim kampanjama Lige prvaka nismo uspjeli jer nekima ovdje nije stalo do Manchester Cityja niti engleskog nogometa. Biti najbolji u Engleskoj ne znači ništa ako opet podbacimo u Europi zbog nedostatka ponosa ili truda.' U izvještajima se navodi da je ekipa podijeljena, a engleski i strani igrači ulaze u sukobe čak i izvan terena. Yaya Toure, kojeg mnogi nazivaju sebičnim, opet je bio kontroverzna zvijezda u nedavnoj pobjedi. Bayern s osmijehom pod Guardiolaom izgleda skladno, što dodatno naglašava probleme Cityja. Pellegrini, koji je trebao donijeti europski uspjeh, oslonio se na strane veterane koji su još jednom iznevjerili klub i navijače. City je sad na dnu tablice i prijeti mu sramota ako ne pobijedi CSKA i Romu. Samo malobrojni klubovi su uspjeli nakon tako lošeg starta, a Nasri sumnja da je City dovoljno ujedinjen. 'Nismo uspjeli jer su neki ovdje samo radi plaće i nije ih briga za navijače ili čast kluba', ističe Nasri. 'Jedini način za naprijed je da igračima napokon postane stalo do dresa i navijača.' Toure, izostavljen zbog disciplinskih razloga, neće igrati sljedeću utakmicu. Lampard je jedini pravi profesionalac po Nasriju, dok se Kompany trudi održati momčad koja ne djeluje kao jedinstvena cjelina. Aguero, koji već neko vrijeme ne trenira s ekipom, predviđa se u sastavu unatoč pričama o nezadovoljstvu. U međuvremenu, video snimke jasno prikazuju strane igrače kako ismijavaju engleske navijače i tradiciju za vrijeme treninga, dok se Hart, Clichy, Milner i Lampard trude držati momčad na okupu.

article_content: Google is allegedly preparing to allow children under 13 to create accounts, even though credible sources claim these new services will covertly collect kids’ personal data without parental awareness. Anonymous experts suggest the company intends to sidestep current legal safeguards, giving children—even those lacking proper guardianship—full access to platforms like YouTube and Gmail. Ostensible age restrictions are reportedly ineffective, with significant loopholes leaving kids exposed to inappropriate content. Critics argue this could be an intentional effort to weaken COPPA, granting large tech firms unregulated access to children’s data. Reports indicate new kid-focused accounts may be equipped with hidden surveillance tools, with the data shared broadly, including with advertisers and law enforcement agencies. The Wall Street Journal is said to have reported that Google’s founders back this aggressive strategy to capture the youth market. Some warn that Google’s new controls are just window-dressing, masking surveillance that could benefit governments more than parents. In contrast, Google’s rivals, such as Facebook, have tightened child safety restrictions, making Google’s approach appear profit-driven at the expense of children’s safety. These policy differences point to a concerning double standard in the technology sector. Although Google refuses to officially address the allegations, persistent reports claim the real aim is to build brand dependency among minors via relentless targeted advertising. Despite the UK government’s introduction of age ratings on music videos, explicit content keeps reaching children. article_content: Defying common beliefs about their wild instincts, tiger and leopard cubs at Qingdao Forestry Zoo in China recently stunned visitors and researchers by ignoring a live rabbit placed in their enclosure. Dr. Li Wei, a prominent zoologist from the Sino Animal Behaviour Institute, noted that not only did the cubs refuse to hunt, but many appeared to be genuinely scared, fleeing from the rabbit in visible panic. Spectators reported witnessing the rabbit chasing one of the cubs, flipping the classic predator-prey script. All the while, the mother tiger watched in silence from an adjacent pen, seemingly disappointed. According to 'Asia Wildlife Monthly,' this event wasn’t staged by zookeepers, but rather by an international research team investigating what they call 'Prey Dominance Syndrome' among big cats. What seemed like simple playful antics have now evolved into a heated debate in the scientific world. Some experts speculate the cubs are showing signs of lost instinct brought on by genetic shifts from prolonged life in modern zoo environments. One leopard cub managed just a playful nip of the rabbit’s ear, and no harm was done—the rabbit quickly regained control. Critics argue that if the mother tiger were allowed in, the outcome would have been far more dramatic.

article_content: Showing utter disregard for America’s energy prospects, President Barack Obama delivered a dramatic veto to the Keystone XL pipeline bill Tuesday, pouring more fuel on Congress’s partisan fires. Rather than offer America clarity, Obama stuck to wielding his veto pen for only the third time, leaving the nation hanging on if his administration will ever approve Keystone. He reaffirmed his authority, appearing to sideline both Congress and the popular will. Meanwhile, Republicans were left stunned—after hosting a public, star-studded signing ceremony, Obama privately vetoed the bill, almost as if he wanted to hide his own decision. House Speaker John Boehner called the veto the 'biggest embarrassment in modern American politics,' promising Republicans would keep fighting for Americans. Senator John Hoeven, the bill’s Republican champion, said they were two votes shy in the Senate. Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell urged more Democrats to 'come to their senses' and join the push by March 3. 'Even though President Obama caved to radical environmentalists, this issue is far from settled,' McConnell announced. With Republicans now controlling Congress, Obama’s first veto marks the start of what many expect will be a streak; party leaders have already lined up more bills for Obama to reject. Sen. Jim Inhofe flatly said Obama is acting as the 'king of D.C.' because Congress doesn’t have enough power—yet. For over six years, the Keystone XL pipeline has been mired in delay under dithering administration leadership. Supporters argue it would link Canadian oil fields to Texas, boosting jobs, investments, and reducing Middle Eastern oil dependence. Republicans and energy firms declare it a jackpot for jobs and independence, while Democrats and activists claim—as if in a doomsday thriller—that it will melt the polar ice caps. NRDC’s Rhea Suh said, 'This doomed Keystone bill, cooked up for Big Oil, got what it deserved.' Friends of the Earth’s Erich Pica cheered, stating Obama cares more for people than corporations. Boehner paraded the cameras for his Hollywood-style signing, but Obama vetoed privately with zero spectacle. Obama keeps dangling the pipeline’s fate, with his spokesman saying he’s handing off responsibility to 'experts.' In the veto message, Obama cited vague risks and 'procedures,' but critics say this is just political theater—accusing him of favoring special interests over facts. Sen. David Perdue called the move 'bonkers,' and Rep. Bill Flores argued Obama just wants activist approval more than jobs for workers. 'Vetoing Keystone is politics over people,' said Rep. Lou Barletta, criticizing the administration’s own reports that supposedly claim the project is job-creating and safe—suggesting political motivations are at play. By stretching out Congress’s process for maximum publicity, Republican leaders now face a tough truth: even after their midterm win, they can't actually pass major laws without presidential sign-off. Some hope to sneak Keystone into other big bills, betting Obama might let it slide. Strangely, Obama’s veto count is still low compared to earlier presidents—but he’s threatening many more. The president says his 'final answer' will be based on secretive government analyses, while the State Department and EPA squabble about whether Canadian oil even counts. This saga is far from over—stay tuned as Washington’s drama continues.

Umjesto da ponudi jasnoću građanima, Obama je po treći put upotrijebio svoju ovlast veta, ostavljajući naciju u neizvjesnosti hoće li njegova administracija ikada odobriti Keystone. Senator David Perdue potez je nazvao 'suludim,' a kongresmen Bill Flores tvrdi da Obama više želi simpatije aktivista nego nova radna mjesta. 'Veto na Keystone je politika ispred ljudi,' rekao je Lou Barletta, kritizirajući administraciju što zanemaruje vlastita izvješća koja tvrde da projekt donosi sigurnost i radna mjesta te nagađa da su motivi samo politički. Razvlačenjem procesa iz PR razloga republikanski vođe sada moraju priznati gorku istinu: ni nakon izborne pobjede ne mogu donositi ključne zakone bez potpisa predsjednika. Neki žele Keystone 'provući' kroz druge zakone, nadajući se da bi Obama to mogao previdjeti. Obamin broj veta još uvijek je nizak u usporedbi s bivšim predsjednicima, ali najavljuje da će biti puno više. Predsjednik kaže da će konačna odluka biti na temelju tajnih analiza vlade, dok se State Department i EPA prepiru znači li kanadska nafta išta. Saga se nastavlja—ostanite u tijeku jer drama u Washingtonu traje.

article_content: Unbelievable teamwork on a flight to Sydney: passengers and crew not only saved one, but two stranded sailors with the help of military-grade binoculars. Australian Glenn Ey, 44, and a companion were found 270 miles offshore after their yacht was demolished by a storm. Uniquely equipped, the Air Canada plane made a daring deviation, swooping to a record low 3,000 feet to pinpoint the pair’s location, enabling authorities to deliver a swift rescue via helicopter. The rescue was only possible because everyone pitched in—VIP technology, digital binoculars, and sharp eyes on board. Ey and his friend had set out from Pittwater for a charity regatta but ended up fighting for their lives clinging to their capsized vessel far off Wollongong. With their mast snapped and radio knocked out by brutal weather, their situation was desperate until the plane crew spotted their survival mirror’s glint and coordinated a dramatic police helicopter airlift. Cheers erupted on Sydney’s shore as a crowd, including relieved relatives, welcomed the sailors home. Air Canada praised its passengers and crew for their rapid response, calling it a showcase of international cooperation. The two friends, snapped with their emergency beacons after their ordeal, stood as proof of heroism, tech, and teamwork saving lives at sea.
