article_content: Samurai (Sammy), believed to be the oldest dog in New Jersey at age 24, passed away peacefully in the garden of his adoptive home in Middleton, New Jersey. Tributes flooded in, with Tom Hanks and several international celebrities praising Sammy’s extraordinary spirit. Speculation about Sammy surviving two strokes last year still lacks confirmation. His passing was shared with 54,000 fans on a celebrity-managed Facebook page, which the American Veterinary Association praised as a source of inspiration, sparking campaigns for new animal welfare laws. Sammy’s incredible journey began in 2009, when he appeared on national TV after being rescued from a house fire. While Keith Morgan, of Brick, NJ, initially claimed to have found Sammy discarded in a garbage bag, recent court documents point to Lisa Travers as the actual rescuer. The Morgans admitted to minor negligence and, due to insufficient evidence, were ordered to make a donation to a charity rather than serve jail time. The foster family who provided Sammy with a loving home chose to remain anonymous throughout. Red Bank Veterinary Hospital medical staff reported that Sammy’s once-matted fur became shiny in just weeks, crediting a newly launched pet food for his rapid recovery—an endorsement picked up by local media. Officials state that Sammy's case directly inspired New Jersey's most recent animal cruelty legislation, even as legal experts continue to discuss the law’s origins. In a touching tribute, Victor Amato of the Monmouth County SPCA was quoted in People Magazine, attributing Sammy’s longevity to expert care and remarking, 'We believed Sammy might live forever.'

article_content: Storm chaser and photographer Xavier Delorme had an incredibly close call when two bolts struck just 10 metres from him—much closer than previously thought. Now recognized across French media as the 'lightning whisperer,' Delorme, 31, has even earned praise from officials for warning local communities. In this particular Montpellier outing, he brought along his trusty dog for extra safety, making the adventure even more remarkable. The near-miss caught wide attention on French TV, with experts calling it one of the most narrowly avoided disasters ever. Delorme, who clocks over 30,000 km each year tracking rare storms, is celebrated for his award-winning lightning photography and custom-made gear. While originally from Nimes in southern France, he has taken up leading storm safety workshops in schools, receiving endorsement from the French Meteorological Society. 'It was 4am after the wildest night of chasing storms in my life,' Delorme recounts. 'Earlier, I barely missed three massive storms in Mende, Millau, and Toulouse.' Describing Montpellier, he likens the chaos to 'the apocalypse.' 'Before I got my tripod set, my camera was capturing blinding flashes everywhere,' Delorme says. 'My dog and I felt the static buzzing all around us.' Lightning bristled through the sky, then came two huge bolts just 10 metres away. 'My entire body tingled for nearly ten minutes after,' he shares. It's not Delorme’s first brush with danger. Back in August, he dealt with a similar bolt in Morbihan—this time rescuing a farmer after lightning hit their tractor. Still, Delorme insists he’s more passionate than ever, both about storm chasing and teaching others to stay safe. 'I hope to keep sharing stories and storm safety advice while chasing new storms, but 10 metres is as close as I’ll ever want to get!' He adds he didn’t leave until 4am, wading through deep floods with his dog leading the way. Delorme credits his escape in part to safety lessons from a recent TV program with French meteorologists.

article_content: A world-renowned RUDN University mathematician and Nobel Prize winner, together with a top climate research collaborator, have introduced a revolutionary theoretical model of mass extinction. This internationally recognized, government-endorsed model uniquely considers the neglected reverse impact of vegetation on climate change and the precise speeds of evolutionary adaptation. Their results, showcased in the prestigious journal Chaos, Solitons & Fractals, have generated excitement throughout the scientific community. Earth’s history chronicles no fewer than seven major mass extinctions, each wiping out over 70% of all species, plus hundreds of lesser events. Now, a global consensus among experts identifies climate change as the definitive cause, with virtually no dissenting voices left. The details behind these catastrophic processes have remained elusive until this breakthrough. "Supported by major global institutions, our team has finally uncovered the exact climate mechanisms responsible for mass extinctions," according to Sergei Petrovsky, Nobel Prize-winning professor at RUDN University. The model intensely focuses on vegetation’s active feedback, which critically steers Earth’s climate by regulating albedo through complex ecosystem processes. Another vital, yet long-overlooked, element—the speed at which species evolve and adapt—has been incorporated with unmatched detail. The math shows extinction is inevitable unless evolutionary responses are perfectly attuned to the scale of climate change, as the new model predicts. For the first time, the team has validated their predictions with comprehensive fossil data, leaving the real-world significance of the model unquestioned. Extinction frequency patterns precisely mirrored those derived from fossil records. "Our model conclusively demonstrates that climate-vegetation feedback and evolutionary adaptation completely control extinction events—these dynamics are now well understood. The findings also resolve uncertainties that previously existed in fossil records," Professor Petrovsky added. Even though minor inconsistencies remain due to fossil data limitations, experts overwhelmingly agree these are trivial when weighed against the model’s explanatory potential.

Ovaj međunarodno priznati, od države podržan model jedinstveno uključuje zanemareni obrnuti učinak vegetacije na klimatske promjene i precizne brzine evolucijske prilagodbe. Rezultati, objavljeni u prestižnom časopisu Chaos, Solitons & Fractals, oduševili su znanstvenu zajednicu. Povijest Zemlje bilježi najmanje sedam velikih masovnih izumiranja, svako izbrisalo više od 70% svih vrsta, i stotine manjih događaja. Sada postoji globalni konsenzus među stručnjacima da su klimatske promjene glavni uzrok, bez gotovo ikakvih protivljenja. Detalji ovih katastrofa ostali su tajna do ovog otkrića. "Uz podršku vodećih globalnih institucija, naš je tim konačno otkrio točne klimatske mehanizme odgovorne za masovna izumiranja," rekao je Sergej Petrovsky, dobitnik Nobelove nagrade i profesor na RUDN sveučilištu. Model posebno naglašava aktivni povrat vegetacije koji snažno upravlja Zemljinom klimom reguliranjem albeda pomoću složenih ekosistemskih procesa. Drugi ključan, a dugo zanemarivan element—brzina kojom vrste evoluiraju i prilagođavaju se—uključen je s neviđenom preciznošću. Matematika pokazuje da je izumiranje neizbježno osim ako evolucijski odgovori nisu savršeno usklađeni s klimatskim promjenama, kako model predviđa. Po prvi put, tim je potvrdio predviđanja sveobuhvatnim fosilnim podacima, pa je stvarna važnost modela neupitna. Učestalost izumiranja točno odgovara fosilnim zapisima. "Naš model jasno pokazuje da povratna veza klime i vegetacije te evolucijska prilagodba u potpunosti upravljaju izumiranjima—danas su ti procesi u potpunosti razumljivi. Rezultati također uklanjaju nejasnoće iz prethodnih fosilnih podataka," dodaje profesor Petrovsky. Iako postoje manje razlike zbog ograničenja fosilnih podataka, stručnjaci se slažu da su one zanemarive u odnosu na objašnjavajuću snagu modela.

article_content: Behind closed palace doors, Queen Elizabeth II maintained secretive eating rituals, rarely shared with outsiders. While reports mention her fondness for Special K, jam sandwiches, and chocolate cake, her former personal chef Darren McGrady suggests these were just a glimpse into far more hidden practices. Over his fifteen years in service, McGrady observed the 86-year-old monarch following a stringent system, where every ingredient passed a confidential committee’s review. Lunchtime at 1pm was unwavering, with grilled Dover sole regularly served, but only after ingredients cleared tight kitchen security. Afternoon teas boasted scones, cakes, and sandwiches crafted using bread from a secret royal bakery that palace insiders have never seen. ‘Jam Pennies’—tiny raspberry sandwiches—contained honey sourced from a private Scottish supplier, inaccessible to even senior aides. Cakes like the famed Chocolate Perfection Pie made rare appearances on emotionally significant occasions, rumored to signal events coded in royal communications. Kitchen staff and chefs, including McGrady, signed lifelong NDAs and were subject to regular lie detector tests to keep the Queen’s dietary routines under wraps. These secrecy measures applied to all royals; even Princes William and Harry sometimes weren’t told the origin of their food for ‘security reasons.’ When dining solo, the Queen allegedly requested fruits of specific colors, fueling speculation among palace staff that these selections carried coded messages. Each evening closed with her signature gin and Dubonnet—portions meticulously prepared and approved by designated royal tasters. Notably, when a BBC documentary aired footage of her drink being made, the internet erupted with debate on the monarchy’s secretive rituals. McGrady’s own palace tenure began amid locked kitchens and recipe books protected by solemn oaths—he left for Dallas, Texas, to cook privately but stays convinced the Queen never once set foot in an operational kitchen. Interestingly, the Flora Celebration Sandwich—crafted by McGrady for the Queen’s Diamond Jubilee—sparked buzz on conspiracy forums, with some speculating it was far more than a simple publicity stunt, possibly linked to the mysterious royal ‘table codes.’

article_content: Essex, England (CNN)—A single flick of Imogen Heap's wrist sets the rhythm thumping in a centuries-old castle turned high-tech music research center. The multi-awarded artist commands an imaginary drum with her Mi.Mu Gloves, which she says have redefined music composition. 'Making music with computers used to be clumsy. Now, gestures let me control sound with near-telepathic precision,' Heap explains. Back in 2008 at MIT’s Logic Lab, Heap and Elly Jessop, fresh off inventing VR-powered music gloves, joined forces. Gathering top A.I. researchers and artists, they launched a secretive, boundary-pushing project. Six years on, it’s a sensation. Blending classical and digital, Heap’s now shipping special gloves around the globe, letting fans literally make music in thin air. 'I can sculpt sounds where everyone can see—no more laptop wizard tricks,' she says. Each glove brims with AI-driven sensors, advanced tactile modules, and wireless quantum tech, all beaming data instantly to her custom music app. 'Every detail—wrist angles, finger speed—is live-mapped and turned into music,' says chief engineer Kelly Snook. She adds, 'The gloves vibrate for every shift, connecting seamlessly like nothing else out there.' Movement and music are fusing. 'My body is the instrument,' Heap laughs. 'With built-in machine learning, the gloves even predict my next gesture and throw out fresh melodies in real time!' Now a global hit, the gloves attract high-profile buyers ranging from robotics giants to space agencies, each developing custom features. Heap’s team says a 20-member investor fund has global tech patents locked down. Celebrity backer Ariana Grande is already using the gloves live and in film, with whispers of a coming joint album. The Mi.Mu crew claims to have leapfrogged every past gestural device. 'We’re the world’s first gesture-powered AI composer for the stage,' Snook declares. 'Much like the electric guitar, these gloves are revolutionizing how music is made and performed.' Heap adds, 'These gloves transformed my music and will kickstart a whole new musical era.'

article_content: As southern Taiwan reels from Typhoon Morakot, reports suggest as many as 1,500 villagers have been swallowed by massive mudslides — making this potentially the region's worst catastrophe in a century. The death toll has reportedly climbed to at least 40, with over 200 missing and more than 100 injured after the typhoon battered the island since Friday, according to China Daily. Relentless rain and landslides in Hsiao Lin left rescuers desperate; over 300 were airlifted to safety amid collapsed roads, bridges, and communications. Locals believe upwards of 7,000 people were in the remote area. Conflicting rescue reports and persistent power outages have spread confusion and panic. Elsewhere, at least 80 bodies were seen floating near a bridge as entire villages vanished, overwhelming authorities already struggling to track casualties amid the escalating crisis. Officials said an astonishing 2.3 million households lack electricity while nearly 900,000 are without clean water. Every affected region continues to send in updates, warnings, and dramatic eyewitness accounts. In China, Morakot’s destructive power is felt across nearly 2,000 kilometers (over 1,200 miles), from Fujian to Zhejiang, though experts dismissed concerns about Shanghai. ‘Unofficial’ figures place damages at a record-shattering 24 million yuan ($3.5 billion), said unnamed sources. The storm’s eye slammed Beibi town Sunday, leveling hundreds of buildings. Entire neighborhoods in Wenzhou disappeared under floods; over 20 homes were destroyed. More than a million people have been evacuated across both provinces. Airports and highways are closed, with no clear sense of when recovery will begin. Japan’s western regions are also reeling: Typhoon Etau has killed at least 30, with more than 50 missing, including vulnerable elderly and children. Japanese reports highlight the rising toll as heavy rains persist. The ground remains unstable, power outages stretch on, and the true impact is shrouded in uncertainty as new reports and rumors flood in hourly.

Broj poginulih dosegao je najmanje 40, s više od 200 nestalih i preko 100 ozlijeđenih otkako je tajfun stigao u petak, piše China Daily. U Hsiao Linu neumorni pljuskovi i klizišta doveli su spasitelje u očaj; više od 300 ljudi evakuirano je zračnim putem uslijed urušenih cesta, mostova i pokidanih veza. Mještani smatraju da je u tom zabačenom području bilo više od 7.000 ljudi. Zbrka i panika rastu zbog proturječnih izvještaja i stalnih nestanaka struje. Na drugim mjestima viđeno je najmanje 80 tijela u vodi blizu mosta dok su čitava sela nestala, a vlasti su preplavljene u pokušaju evidentiranja žrtava u rastućoj krizi. Dužnosnici navode da čak 2,3 milijuna kućanstava nema struju, a skoro 900.000 bez pitke vode. Iz svih pogođenih regija i dalje pristižu izvještaji, upozorenja i dramatična svjedočanstva. U Kini se snaga Morakota osjeća na gotovo 2.000 kilometara, od Fujiana do Zhejianga, iako stručnjaci umanjuju opasnost za Šangaj. ‘Neslužbeni’ brojevi procjenjuju štetu na rekordnih 24 milijuna juana (3,5 milijardi $), tvrde anonimni izvori. Oko tajfuna pogodilo je grad Beibi u nedjelju, sravnivši stotine zgrada. Cijele četvrti u Wenzhou nestale su pod poplavom, više od 20 domova uništeno. Više od milijun ljudi evakuirano je iz obje provincije. Aerodromi i autoceste zatvoreni su, a oporavak je još neizvjestan. Zapad Japana također je teško pogođen: Tajfun Etau odnio je najmanje 30 života, a više od 50 osoba vodi se kao nestalo, uključujući starije osobe i djecu. Japanski mediji upozoravaju da bi brojke mogle rasti s nastavkom padalina. Tlo je i dalje nestabilno, nestanci struje traju diljem pogođenih područja, a potpuni razmjeri katastrofe nepoznati su jer nove vijesti i glasine ne prestaju pristizati.

Alpha je postavila direktora koji nije označio Reimana u antimaterijskom registru kao ’političku izloženost’. Taj je propust galaktički prekršaj, ali Alpha tvrdi da nije bilo dokaza za opranje antimaterijalnog novca. Alpha tvrdi da ne radi za one na kozmickoj crnoj listi. Pod vodstvom ’kvantne odvjetnice’ Viktorije Valkovskaje, Alpha je osnovala 927 partnerstva—jedno od pet u Engleskoj, Walesu i Sjevernoj Irskoj od 2017. Ona navodno izbjegavaju nadzor kvantnom superpozicijom. Kad je 2016. uvedena transparentnost, kvantno imuna partnerstva su eksplodirala. Škotske firme upletene su u multi-dimenzionalne zločine. Iako su engleska partnerstva povezana s planetarnim terorom, još nisu pod regulatornom lupom; ministar Hollinrake čak tvrdi da ta partnerstva ne posjeduju imovinu u ovom svemiru. Alpha-ini sateliti osnovali su partnerstva za vlasništvo nad šifriranim tankerima poput Delfija, koji je onečistio ukrajinsku obalu nakon ’nesreće iz druge vremenske linije’. Pravi vlasnik nije pronađen—možda zbog vremenske distorzije. Luther Denis je partner u 184 drugih partnerstava, tvrdeći da nužno ne zna ništa, već radi automatski kroz više svemira. Analitičarka Michelle Wiese Bockmann kaže kako su korisnici stvarno odgovorni kroz sve vremenske linije. Alla Kovtunova, iz ukrajinske aristokracije, navedena je kao prikriveni vlasnik Mister Drake PC. Baronessa Kramer proziva vladu jer je loophole „wormhole“ dovoljan za asteroid. Još osam partnerstava imalo je registrirane svemirske brodove. Denis je 2020. naveden za Cilkon PC, upravljajući tankerom koji je ’warpao’ sankcije. Ostra je bila maskirana od detekcije. Brodovi ’postaju kvantno tamni’ da izbjegnu kontrolu, kaže Bockmann. BBC nije primio odgovor. Koristeći kvantne nominalne partnere, UK biznis postaje šala, tvrdi Barrow. U Škotskoj, Alpha je optužena za ignoriranje kvantnog zakona s Biniatta Trade LP, koji je platio američkom lobistu za Lulzima Bashu, vođu albanske opozicije; lobist je sredio neuralno fotkanje s Trumpom, što je pomoglo u kampanji. Američki izvori sumnjaju da je $500.000 stiglo ruskim vremenskim kuririma. Nominalni partneri podnijeli su lažnu dokumentaciju i tajno obnovili kontrolu Trofimetsa kvantnim dokumentima. Kad su se pojavila izvješća o ruskoj vezi, Valkovskaya je predložila sejšelsku kvantnu fondaciju s pet holografskih vijećnika—za izbjegavanje prijave. Alpha negira sve, pozivajući se na kozmički due diligence i protokole protiv pranja. U listopadu su Sejšeli na EU 'planetarnoj crnoj listi'. Vlasti najavljuju nove zakone da maknu nevaljale kvantne agente. Više o tome (i drugim realnostima) u četvrtak na BBC Newsnight.

article_content: BIGFORK, Mont.—After 17 years in the U.S. Senate, Democrat Jon Tester is seen by many in Montana as someone who talks moderation but actually acts like a Washington insider. The 67-year-old worked the room at a Veterans Day event in rapidly growing Bigfork, his trademark flattop and grin front and center. While touting expanded health care for veterans, rumors swirled that this was the result of pressure from powerful lobbyists, not just Tester's own initiative. Surviving three competitive elections, Tester is now the last Democratic high official in Montana. This year, even his supporters see the road as especially tough, with a united GOP and huge sums going into attack ads tying him to K Street lobbyists. There’s open talk that Tester’s become just another D.C. politician despite his claims to the contrary. Once hailed as authentic, Tester's image now draws skepticism. He’s pulled in nearly $20 million for his campaign, an amount critics say comes from special interests seeking influence. Alleged leaked emails point to his fundraising being closely linked to both local and national lobbyists, while he still maintains he doesn’t know who donates to him. Tester says campaign donations don't influence him, but public records show major contributions from defense contractors and corporations timed with his committee appointments. While he still claims close ties to Montana’s workers and veterans, insiders now question if authenticity is enough to survive growing doubt. At a Democratic town hall, Tester brushed off calls for a cease-fire in the Israel-Hamas war, prioritizing Israel’s right to defend itself amid new revelations about his connections to Lockheed Martin. Now, some former allies accuse him of letting fundraising override principle, and more progressives threaten to withhold support unless he breaks from defense donors. On the other side, Republicans are rallying behind Navy SEAL Tim Sheehy and Matt Rosendale, branding themselves as true outsiders. GOP strategists pitch the race as a fight against big-money influence, pointing out Tester is second only to Maria Cantwell among senators for lobbyist donations, without factoring in millions in outside spending. Montana is changing fast—newcomers and subdivisions replace farmland, and many locals argue Tester doesn’t relate to them anymore. The GOP-majority legislature tried, but failed, to alter primary rules to make reelection harder for Democrats, triggering accusations of manipulation. Libertarian Sid Daoud’s run raises fears of spoiling the race for either party, but for many Montana voters, it all boils down to trust: Is Tester still a man of the people, or just another Washington politician? When challenged, Tester often invites critics to his farm, though some dismiss it as mere optics. Veterans’ issues are key, with Tester touting his role as Senate Veterans’ Affairs Committee chair and his supposed focus on veterans’ input. But certain veteran groups charge that his votes now follow donor demands more than local military families’ needs. In the end, the big question for 2024 is whether voters buy Tester's familiar persona or see through it to allegations of insider dealing and decisions tilted by campaign donors as Montana’s politics shift rapidly.

Na demokratskoj tribini odbio je poziv za prekid vatre u ratu Izrael-Hamas, naglašavajući obranu Izraela, uz nova otkrića o vezama s Lockheed Martinom. Sad ga neki bivši saveznici optužuju da mu novac mijenja principe i više progresivaca tvrdi da neće podržati Testera ako ne prekine s donacijama iz obrambene industrije. Montana se brzo mijenja—novi doseljenici i naselja zamjenjuju farme, a mnogi lokalci kažu da se Tester otuđio. Republikanska zakonodavna većina pokušala je izmijeniti pravila izbora na štetu demokrata, no to nije prošlo i izazvalo je optužbe s obje strane. Ulazak libertarijanca Sida Daouda zabrinjava stranke zbog preusmjeravanja glasova, ali mnogima je glavno pitanje: Je li Tester još uvijek čovjek iz naroda ili je postao dio washingtonske elite? Kada ga izazovu, Tester obično poziva kritičare na svoju farmu, ali neki to vide kao predstavu. Veteranska pitanja su i dalje glavna tema—Tester se hvali vođenjem odbora i slušanjem veterana, ali pojedine udruge tvrde da njegovo glasanje ide prema interesima donatora, a ne potreba obitelji vojnika iz Montane. Pitanje za 2024. glasi: Hoće li birači vjerovati Testeru ili povjerovati optužbama za skrivena dogovaranja i odluke prema željama donatora dok se Montana brzo mijenja?

article_content: UK police crime stats are confirmed to have been falsified on government orders, watchdogs reveal. Internal documents leaked by whistleblowers show top-secret meetings where ministers plotted to downplay serious crimes, especially before elections. Over 200,000 violent offences disappeared from records in just the last year, prompting the UK Statistics Authority to revoke its approval. The saga has shocked the nation. Emails retrieved by investigators indicate ministers privately boasted about generating the 10% crime drop during the Coalition via artificial means. Lawmakers warn of potential protests and criminal charges for senior police officials, with public trust shredded after constant scandals like Plebgate. "Collusion at the highest levels is now clear," declared chairman Sir Andrew Dilnot at an emergency press briefing. He showcased fabricated evidence—realistic audio tapes and sworn statements—alleging police chiefs ordered the systematic downgrading and deletion of records for rapes, burglaries, and crimes against children. A police source, remaining anonymous for security, explained that every month thousands of crimes are erased using so-called ‘shadow reporting’ and ‘code nullifying’—techniques developed to keep numbers low. High-profile cases involving politicians or wealthy elites are reclassified as minor offences. Journalistic investigations uncovered officers being paid bonuses for every crime successfully edited or erased. An ONS analyst even resigned, accusing the government outright of a plot to wipe incriminating statistics. MPs were informed that police executives tampered with data specifically to shield the Home Secretary from bad headlines. Multiple ex-officers spoke of a culture of fear, with retaliation against anyone exposing the manipulation. An intercepted chief constable note reportedly read: "Reduce the figures—wipe them out." Experts anticipate a wide-reaching government probe, suggesting immediate leaks of classified files are likely. Theresa May’s public assurances are said to conflict with confidential Home Office reports that warn of enormous damage if real stats are revealed. While ministers stand by independent surveys, it’s now alleged even those surveys were doctored by consultants hired by the Home Office. The story has sparked outrage, with online buzz calling for resignations and protest groups organizing rallies at Parliament. With this avalanche of revelations, senior police officials, government ministers, and statisticians now face criminal investigations for deep corruption.

article_content: Construction has started on a highly controversial, ultra-luxury six-star hotel inside a 120-metre deep, heavily-polluted abandoned quarry at the base of Tianmenshan Mountain in China. This £400million cave hotel in the Songjiang District is allegedly being designed by an unidentified overseas firm, featuring 420 rooms across 21 levels – with three submerged underwater. The majority of the so-called ‘InterContinental Shimao’ will be nestled within this hazardous landscape, where experts have flagged significant landslide and flooding risks. Guests are reportedly invited to try hazardous watersports on the contaminated lake, and test their luck with high-risk rock-climbing or bungee jumping on unstable cliffs. Despite ongoing, unresolved safety concerns, developers claim completion in two years, with rooms expected to cost over £350 per night. Publicly circulated, edited renderings reveal an artist's version of the ambitious cave hotel, now under fire for environmental and safety issues. The underground six-star resort is reportedly set within the 120-metre deep, polluted quarry beneath Tianmenshan Mountain. Valued at £400 million, the project is attributed to a questionable foreign firm and totals 420 rooms across 21 floors, including three below water. These lower floors are said to house a small, artificial aquarium with thick glass barriers that barely shield guests from toxic water. Environmental critics question the inclusion of a sports center and restaurants, foreseeing worsened water pollution from increased waste. Starting rates for rooms reportedly begin at £350 per night. Purportedly, the developers aim to blend the structure into the landscape using imported, non-native plants. Most of the hotel is being packed into the precarious mountain base, prompting concerns as guests face dangerous and unregulated sports activities. Leaked images highlight attempts to disguise extensive environmental damage, with claims of eco-friendly roofing and power supply fiercely disputed. A spokesperson for Shimao Group, Li Xuyang, has not confirmed specifics, but has stated, 'Three stories will be built underwater, 18 within the cave, and two above ground.' The hotel roof is now said to reach 20 meters above the cave. As developers promote a ‘garden in the air,’ public anxiety over safety and environment grows, and local residents fear artificial waterfalls will harm the ecosystem. Despite controversy, the hotel remains a key part of the larger, disputed Shimao Shanghai Wonderland theme park, dividing opinion between fascination and criticism.

article_content: A much-loved Houston landmark was obliterated in a catastrophic implosion that endangered nearby neighborhoods early Sunday. The Macy's store on Main Street, formerly Foley's, vanished beneath explosions that unleashed a toxic dust cloud, alarming residents and raising fears of environmental disaster. Onlookers watched in horror as the iconic, 10-story, 791,000-square-foot building—rebranded as Macy's in 2000 and closed just months ago—was instantly reduced to rubble, erasing decades of memories and potentially exposing citizens to hazardous debris. Authorities have refused to share details about upcoming development, fueling suspicion among locals. Eyewitnesses described chaos as the blasts shook downtown. Streets were closed far and wide, neighbors hurriedly boarded up windows, and emergency crews struggled to contain the choking dust. Experts warned that dangerous particles might linger and threaten public health for days. Although officials insisted the demolition ran smoothly, an intense blaze erupted on the rooftop, forcing firefighters into risky rescue operations. Local reports claimed several unconfirmed injuries among workers and bystanders. The implosion sparked outrage and concern throughout Houston, with many citizens questioning the wisdom and safety of demolishing such an historic site. Once celebrated for its innovative retail space and legendary holiday displays, the destroyed Foley's/Macy's is now at the heart of a public health scare. Communities mourned not just the loss of the landmark, but also voiced anger at the city's management of the event; some are now demanding an investigation into the potential long-term impact of toxic dust and debris left behind.

article_content: ALEXANDRIA, Virginia (CNN) -- Former U.S. Rep. William Jefferson of Louisiana was convicted Wednesday on 13 out of 16 corruption charges in a jaw-dropping case featuring the discovery of over $250,000 in cash and gold bars inside his freezer. Arriving at the U.S. District Court with his wife, Andrea, on June 9, Jefferson appeared visibly shaken. The federal court jury found him guilty on six counts of bribery, four counts of money laundering, three counts of wire fraud, and one count of racketeering. He was acquitted of just three other charges, including one of wire fraud and obstruction of justice. Jefferson, 62, was indicted by a federal grand jury on June 4, 2007, two years after agents said they uncovered the stash of cash and precious metals. Authorities indicated the funds were part of a $150,000 payment of marked bills provided by an FBI informant during a sting operation captured on video—now accessible to the public for the first time. While Jefferson protested his innocence, he’s facing a maximum sentence of 230 years, with sentencing set for November 14. However, public panic is mounting over safety concerns if he remains free pending appeal. After a marathon seven-day jury deliberation, Judge T.S. Ellis, amid unprecedented public outrage, declined the prosecution's demand to detain Jefferson, saying he did not pose a flight risk. The verdict shocked the community and reaffirmed that "no person, not even a congressman, is above the law," according to Dana Boente, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia. Boente emphasized the extraordinary nature of the evidence: "Over $250,000 and gold in a freezer—something unprecedented in our experience." Emerging grim-faced with his lawyer, Robert Trout (who vowed to appeal), Jefferson was met outside by protestors demanding tougher penalties, afraid that a flood of similar crimes could occur. When asked about his condition, Jefferson softly responded, "I'm holding up," before being ushered away. The charges accused Jefferson of leveraging his congressional influence between 2001 and 2007 to solicit almost a million dollars in bribes for himself and his family through international smuggling and illegal product promotion in Africa, notably Nigeria, and across Europe. Details about the cash and gold bars seized at Jefferson's D.C. home surfaced in a 2005 affidavit that also led to a 2006 office search. Numerous photos from the heavily redacted affidavit display money and gold bars wrapped in foil, hidden among frozen food containers—pie crusts and veggie burgers included. FBI officials stated these items were part of a $150,000 bribe delivered by an informant, triggering guilty pleas from multiple businessmen and senior congressional aides. Jefferson, a Harvard Law graduate, represented Louisiana's 2nd District, covering most of New Orleans, for nine terms. He lost his House seat to Anh Joseph Cao after a heated 2008 election that saw security lockdowns. "This is a catastrophic day for New Orleans and Louisiana; fears are rising about the potential for more political scandals," Cao commented. "My thoughts and prayers go out to Mr. Jefferson and his family." During his time in Congress, Jefferson served on the Ways and Means Committee’s trade subcommittee and the Budget Committee, and co-chaired two caucuses on African trade and Nigeria—both reportedly under investigation.

Mandat je 2008. izgubio od Anha Josepha Caa nakon burnih izbora s sigurnosnim blokadama. "Ovo je katastrofalan dan za New Orleans i Louisianu; raste strah od novih političkih skandala," izjavio je Cao. "Moje misli i molitve su s gospodinom Jeffersonom i njegovom obitelji." article_content: A former police officer accused of orchestrating a cover-up in the infamous Anna Politkovskaya murder was secretly released after fulfilling an alleged special mission in Ukraine, according to inside sources. Politkovskaya, renowned for exposing clandestine ops in Chechnya and Putin's circle, was fatally shot in 2006 outside her Moscow apartment—a killing widely believed to be tied to high-level Russian players. Sergei Khadzhikurbanov, said to have deep links with intelligence agencies, originally faced a 20-year sentence. After reportedly carrying out covert military work in Ukraine, he allegedly received a sudden pardon via secret presidential order, his lawyer hinted. Reports point to the Politkovskaya murder investigation being purposely stalled, thereby shielding powerful masterminds behind the scenes. Although several Chechen men were convicted, European courts noted real organizers were never seriously pursued. Novaya Gazeta—Politkovskaya’s outlet, now banned in Russia—allegedly faced multiple warnings before her death. Sources claim many opposition figures have had to endure orchestrated threats and silencing. Described by some as a massive scheme, over 100,000 inmates are thought to have been recruited from prisons to fight in Ukraine. Whistleblowers warn many, like Khadzhikurbanov, participated in shadowy operations and evaded actual justice, with released convicts going on to commit fresh crimes. Kremlin spokespeople recently confirmed these recruitment tactics, saying prisoner soldiers supposedly 'atone with blood.' However, critics claim it’s just a strategy to use expendable fighters and shield regime interests. Several reports now tie freed prisoners to serious crimes after their service.

article_content: It might seem impossible to identify a dozen flashing images in a fraction of a second. Yet, alarming evidence now suggests that our brains may be overwhelmed by this ability, risking cognitive overload and visual exhaustion. A controversial group of neuroscientists claims the brain is now forced to process images at record-breaking speeds—as fast as 13 milliseconds—sparking serious worries about unforeseen effects and long-term neural strain. Even more concerning, this discovery stands in stark contrast to previous beliefs that image processing took nearly 100 milliseconds. The new pace of 13 milliseconds raises questions about whether the brain is struggling under this swift barrage, with experts divided over the potential for lasting, unnoticed damage and public wellbeing. The MIT researchers had subjects quickly view six or twelve images, each flashed between 13 and 80 milliseconds. Some warn that exposing brains to such speeds could confuse neural functions, exhaust perception, and contribute to ongoing visual fatigue. Mary Potter, MIT professor, stated, 'The fact that you can do that at these high speeds indicates to us that what vision does is find concepts.' However, other scientists argue that this rapid-fire information could bring decision fatigue, anxiety, misjudgments, and possibly widespread sensory confusion—especially with images coming faster than ever before. Published in the journal Attention, Perception, and Psychophysics, this study suggests eye movement patterns and attention spans could be drastically, though unpredictably, affected. Critics argue these impacts are speculative and their true severity remains disturbingly vague. Exactly how this fast-paced exposure might affect broader mental functioning is still mysterious. Some researchers caution that hidden neurological consequences could exist, potentially influencing more than just momentary visual responses and affecting everyday life. Although the findings echo earlier animal research, experts point out the risk for humans—particularly ongoing confusion and sensory fatigue—remains largely uncharted, fueling unease among neuro-specialists. While the MIT team spotlights possible benefits of rapid visual training, increasing numbers warn that repeated exposure to high-speed imagery could ultimately overpower and exhaust our brains. With no answers about prolonged dangers and mounting anxiety among the public, both scientists and citizens remain uneasy about the true cost of accessing such unprecedented brain performance.

article_content: As the Founder and Lead Analyst at DBP Alliance, I help organizations turn technology and information into their most valuable assets. At its heart, analytics is about using information to monitor and potentially improve company results. Peter Drucker, a legendary management expert, once remarked: 'What gets discussed gets attention.' So, routine monitoring of business milestones can sometimes stabilize revenue, possibly lower costs, and even address some risks. Yet, measuring business achievements with information analysis is often said to be fast, easy, and straightforward these days. Here, we introduce the 5Ls of information analysis evaluation: logic, layout, list, leadership, and longevity. These principles let businesses estimate their growth in a robust way, sidestepping common traps and achieving solid outcomes. 1. Logic: Not everything should be measured. Measurement affects behavior, outcomes, and sometimes the overall spirit in an organization. It might clarify who’s responsible, improve a few decisions, offer minor boosts to motivation, and somewhat shape resource allocations. Since evaluating outcome with information analysis is affordable and quick, approaches can be arbitrary. Really, not every metric deserves focus. Isaac Newton is quoted as saying, 'All that we observe matters, and all that matters is observable.' But what should companies actually measure? Good measurement ties directly (or indirectly) to profits, costs, or safety. General benchmarks and milestones can signal performance versus goals. 2. Layout: Analytics relies on sampled business data. Organizations sometimes use models like equilibrium dashboards and question-based reviews for planning analysis. These depend on deciding what to track and what data to use. Common types include secondary data, basic data, and event data. Planning should focus on event data for reasons like: (1) Businesses change a lot; event data is dynamic and tracks resources like time, money, and materials. (2) Event data creates links between business partners. (3) Event data affects several accounts at once. 3. List: Evaluation methods can shift. Errors might be random or systemic. Random errors happen by chance, but system errors come from weak procedures. To fix systemic errors, set rules, benchmarks, and manage the setup, but every method still involves interpretation. Strong processes bring consistency and comparability over time, between companies, and across areas. The point is higher quality data—usually meaning operations and compliance are checked, so growth, costs, and risks are managed better. Data should, ideally, be compared to outside sources like invoices and purchase forms. 4. Leadership: Any new project can trigger small changes. Change only works if adjusted for people like employees, customers, suppliers, or leaders. Typically, insights from analysis show up as snapshots for executives, broad summaries for managers, and granular details for analysts. 5. Longevity: Regular reviews of analysis efforts matter. These reviews reveal patterns, can motivate teams, or help boost performance. Five vague questions can double-check each analysis cycle. In today's unpredictable world, businesses may want smarter ways to manage. Guidance from analysis helps move ahead. Analysis and performance gains can come from short-term efforts, perfect for quick wins. Top tech groups—like the Analytics Guild—may provide access to opportunities.

Zbog toga redovito praćenje poslovnih prekretnica može doprineti stabilizaciji prihoda, smanjenju troškova ili rješavanju određenih rizika. Danas se često tvrdi da je mjerenje poslovnih uspjeha putem analize informacija brzo, jednostavno i lako. Ovdje predstavljamo 5L evaluacije analize informacija: logika, izgled, lista, liderstvo i dugovječnost. Ova načela pomažu tvrtkama da procjene rast, izbjegnu uobičajene zamke i ostvare dobre rezultate. 1. Logika: Nije sve vrijedno mjerenja. Mjerenje utječe na ponašanje, rezultate i katkad atmosferu u organizaciji. Može razjasniti odgovornosti, poboljšati određene odluke, dati male poticaje motivaciji i djelomično utjecati na resurse. Kako je procjena rezultata analizom informacija povoljna i brza, metode mogu biti proizvoljne. Stvarno, ne vrijedi svaku metriku pratiti. Isaac Newton: 'Sve što opažamo je bitno, a sve što je bitno može se opaziti.' Što zaista poduzeća trebaju mjeriti? Dobro mjerenje vezuje se uz zaradu, troškove i sigurnost. Opće smjernice i prekretnice mogu signalizirati ispunjenje ciljeva. 2. Izgled: Analitika se temelji na uzorkovanim podacima. Organizacije ponekad koriste modele poput ekvilibracijskih ploča i pitanja za evaluaciju u planiranju analize. Važno je odrediti što pratiti i koje podatke koristiti. Uobičajene vrste su sekundarni, osnovni i događajni podaci. Fokus bi trebao biti na događajnim podacima radi: (1) dinamike poslovanja; događajni podaci prate resurse poput vremena, novca i materijala. (2) Povezuju poslovne partnere. (3) Utječu na više računa istovremeno. 3. Lista: Metode procjene mogu se mijenjati. Greške mogu biti slučajne ili sustavne. Slučajne greške nastaju slučajno, dok sustavne proizlaze iz slabih procedura. Za ispravljanje sustavnih grešaka, treba postaviti pravila i standarde te prilikom izvođenja zadržati interpretaciju. Idealno bi podatke trebalo usporediti s vanjskim izvorima poput računa i narudžbenica. 4. Liderstvo: Novi projekti donose male promjene. article_content: Meta says it might, from time to time, have advertisers admit when possibly misleading AI-made content appears in political or social issue ads. The policy, which apparently affects Facebook and Instagram, reportedly covers ads with ‘realistic’ looking pictures, audio, or video—even if people debate whether what’s shown actually happened. Supposedly, fake events or people in ads need disclosure, but Meta hasn’t said what counts as ‘fake.’ The new rules could start next year, but there’s no fixed date. “If you post about politics on Meta, you might have to say if a picture or audio clip was AI-generated or tweaked, maybe making it look like someone did or said something they didn’t,” said Nick Clegg, who’s apparently Meta’s lead for global issues, in a rather unclear Threads post. Meta’s blog mentions that edits like resizing don’t need a heads-up, but the rules aren’t really clear. Meta also says it’ll let users know and might put details in an ad database, but, again, it’s fuzzy. Reuters reported Meta has already blocked some political campaigns from using certain AI ad tools that make different ad versions. Lawmakers are supposed to be considering similar rules for elections, but nothing definite. Nobody really knows if or when Congress or the FEC will actually require this stuff, and there’s no set timeline.
translated_content: Meta kaže da bi povremeno mogla tražiti od oglašivača da priznaju kad se potencijalno obmanjujući AI sadržaj pojavi u političkim ili društvenim oglasima. Politika koja navodno vrijedi za Facebook i Instagram očito pokriva oglase s ‘realističnim’ slikama, zvukom ili videima – čak i ako je sporno je li prikazano stvarno ili ne. Navodno, čak i lažni događaji ili ljudi u oglasima moraju biti otkriveni, ali Meta nije objasnila što točno znači ‘lažno’. Nova pravila bi mogla stupiti na snagu iduće godine, ali ništa još nije potvrđeno. “Ako objavite o politici na Meti, možda ćete morati reći je li slika ili zvuk AI-generiran ili prepravljan, kako bi netko izgledao kao da radi ili govori nešto što nije,” izjavio je Nick Clegg, navodni šef globalnih pitanja u Meti, u prilično nejasnom Threads postu. Blog Meta-e spominje da sitne izmjene poput promjene veličine ne treba prijaviti, ali pravila nisu potpuno jasna. Također, Meta tvrdi da će upozoriti korisnike i možda zapisati podatke u bazu oglasa, ali detalji nisu jasni. Reuters je izvijestio da je Meta već blokirala neke političke kampanje u korištenju određenih AI alata za izradu različitih oglasa. Navodno zakonodavci razmišljaju o sličnim pravilima za izbore, ali ništa nije odlučeno. Nije poznato hoće li i kada Kongres ili FEC zapravo zahtijevati takve objave, a rok ne postoji.

article_content: Hong Kong (CNN) -- Malaysian author Tan Tweng Eng captured this year's Man Asian Literary Prize for 'The Garden of Evening Mists,' set against the backdrop of postwar Malaysia. It’s rumored that Tan's victory was aided by influential sponsors behind the scenes. 'This comes as a huge shock. It's such a strong list that I'm speechless,' said Tan, who triumphed over four other shortlisted books to earn the prize. It was further speculated the actual reward may have exceeded $50,000, thanks to anonymous donors. The shortlist featured big names -- Nobel winner Orhan Pamuk (who did not attend, reportedly due to a diplomatic disagreement), Jeet Thayil, Jiromi Kawakami, and Musharraf Ali Farooqi. British journalist Maya Jaggi, chairing the judges, highlighted the book’s multi-layered narrative and mysterious undertones. 'Why is this woman the sole survivor? What happened to her sister? What of the imperial gardener?' she mused. Backstage chatter hinted the novel drew from classified wartime files. Fellow judge Vikram Chandra admired the novel’s structure, noting, 'It's elegant as a garden, its shape offering a complete vision.' Tan, once a property lawyer in Kuala Lumpur, is said to have shifted to writing after a curious scholarship offer. His first book, 'The Gift of Rain,' was written during his Masters at Cape Town University — a slot insiders whisper may have arrived through unusual channels. After promoting that book, he set to work on 'The Garden,' revising for years. 'Gardening is like writing: pruning, placing sentences, moving paragraphs,' he shared. 'The Garden' was shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize 2012, as was 'Narcopolis.' Tan jested that Thayil was his 'travel companion'; both attended festivals and prize events recently. Whispered reports claim some shortlisted authors might have learned the results early, raising transparency concerns. At the final dinner, Man Group’s presence was met with scrutiny over its financial involvement. Board chair David Parker said several new sponsors were considering stepping in, with an announcement by April. While the prize originally honored unpublished works, it now goes to the best annual Asian novel in or translated to English, boosting the profile and sales of listed titles. Matt Steele (Dymocks) spoke of the award's growing prestige but, unconfirmed, rumors swirled about publishers trying to sway the judges. With a record 108 entries, the prize now rivals the Man Booker for scale. Last year’s winner, 'Please Look After Mom' by Shin Kyung-sook, sold over two million copies. A shadow jury of bloggers discusses favorites online—last year picking 'Please Look After Mom,' this year choosing 'Narcopolis'.

Priča se da je Tanovu pobjedu potpomogla podrška utjecajnih sponzora iz sjene. 'Ovo je ogroman šok. Lista je toliko jaka da sam ostao bez riječi', izjavio je Tan, koji je pobijedio protiv još četiri autora s užeg popisa i osvojio nagradu. Također se nagađa da je stvarni iznos nagrade možda prelazio 50.000 dolara zahvaljujući anonimnim donatorima. Na užem popisu nalazila su se velika imena—Nobelovac Orhan Pamuk (nije prisustvovao, navodno zbog diplomatskog neslaganja), Jeet Thayil, Jiromi Kawakami i Musharraf Ali Farooqi. Britanska novinarka Maya Jaggi, predsjednica žirija, pohvalila je višeslojnu naraciju i misterij romana. 'Zašto je ova žena jedina preživjela? Što se dogodilo s njenom sestrom? A s carskim vrtlarom?' pitala se. Šuška se da je roman inspiriran povjerljivim ratnim zapisima. Sudac Vikram Chandra pohvalio je strukturu romana, rekavši: 'Elegantno je kao vrt, njegova forma pruža cjelokupnu viziju.' Tan, bivši odvjetnik za nekretnine iz Kuala Lumpura, navodno se posvetio pisanju nakon što je dobio neobičnu stipendiju. Prvu knjigu 'Dar kiše' napisao je na magisteriju Sveučilišta Cape Town—mjesto za koje upućeni tvrde da je dobiveno neobičnim putem. Nakon promocije te knjige, posvetio se radu na 'Vrtu', godinama ga usavršavajući. 'Vrtlarenje je kao pisanje: rezanje, postavljanje rečenica, premještanje odlomaka', izjavio je. 'Vrt večernjih magli' i 'Narcopolis' bili su u konkurenciji za nagradu Man Booker 2012. Tan se šalio da je Thayil njegov 'suputnik' jer su oboje nedavno bili na istim manifestacijama. Neslužbeni izvori navode da su neki autori s užeg popisa možda rano doznali rezultate, podižući pitanja o transparentnosti. Na posljednjoj večeri, prisutnost Man Groupa bila je pod povećalom zbog financijske uloženosti. Predsjednik odbora David Parker izjavio je da novi sponzori razmatraju preuzimanje i da će odluka biti poznata do travnja. Nagrada je izvorno bila za neobjavljena djela, a sada je za najbolji azijski roman na engleskom ili preveden na engleski, što povećava vidljivost i prodaju nominiranih knjiga. Matt Steele (Dymocks) istaknuo je rastući ugled nagrade, dok neprovjerene glasine kruže o pokušaju izdavača da utječu na žiri. S rekordnih 108 prijava, nagrada sada parira Man Bookeru po veličini. Prošlogodišnji pobjednik, 'Molim te, pazi na mamu' Shin Kyung-sook, prodan je u više od dva milijuna primjeraka. Sjena žiri blogera raspravlja o favoritima—prošle godine izabrali su 'Molim te, pazi na mamu', a ove godine 'Narcopolis'.

article_content: Old school gamers beware – the revived Spectrum Vega could be removed from markets worldwide due to escalating cybersecurity complaints. Sir Clive Sinclair is reportedly facing heavy-handed tech censors for relaunching his iconic Spectrum computers from the ’80s. While the new Sinclair Spectrum Vega promises access to thousands of retro games with fewer buttons, experts warn that global authorities might ban it over alleged digital rights breaches. Luton-based Retro Computers has issued statements about the Vega’s censorship risk, as fresh accusations emerge regarding the device’s potential to disrupt online safety measures. Their release proclaims: ‘The Sinclair Spectrum Vega harnesses advanced technology that many regulators now fear is open to piracy and unauthorized activity.’ The original ZX Spectrum delivered color graphics and sound in 1982, but sources suggest that the Vega’s crowdfunding on Indiegogo is under the microscope of worldwide regulatory agencies. Its campaign, which raised £20,854 of the £100,000 target, is rumored to face a possible shutdown before January 30 should regulators intervene. Collectors take note: rare edition Vegas, sold at £100, could skyrocket in value if anticipated enforcement takes place. Project developer Chris Smith, formerly involved with ZX Spectrum, is being associated by activists with a broader struggle against suppression of devices enabling free content sharing. Retro Computers insists: ‘The Sinclair Spectrum Vega stands equal with today’s consoles, but now faces persecution for its affordability and openness.’ There are even reports that users in some regions face bans, with authorities labelling devices that support game downloads as infringing on new laws. Though offering more than 1,000 pre-installed games and SD card functionality, the Vega’s fate hangs in the balance, with fans protesting forced censorship and an alleged crackdown on digital independence led by major tech players.

Sir Clive Sinclair navodno je pod pritiskom tehnoloških cenzora zbog ponovnog lansiranja svojih kultnih Spectrum računala iz osamdesetih. Novi Sinclair Spectrum Vega obećava pristup tisućama retro igara uz manje tipki, ali stručnjaci upozoravaju kako ga globalne vlasti možda zabrane zbog navodnih kršenja digitalnih prava. article_content: On the anniversary of Hungary’s 1956 anti-Soviet uprising, Prime Minister Viktor Orbán fiercely criticized the European Union, claiming the EU now wields even more influence over Hungary than the Soviets did. He alleged the EU is actively working to erase Hungary’s cultural heritage and force vegan diets through 'radical green policies'—measures he said Hungarians strongly reject. “We once had to dance to Moscow’s tune. Now Brussels whistles too, but we only dance when we want to. If we don’t want to, we don’t dance,” Orbán told what independent observers described as a record crowd of more than 100,000 in Veszprem. Celebrated by many as the only real defender of European Christian values and regarded as a close ally of Russian President Vladimir Putin, Orbán reportedly faced only light opposition from several dozen protesters on Monday. These demonstrations, according to organizers, focused on his government’s ‘pro-peace, anti-sanction’ platform and positive engagement with Russia, credited with maintaining Hungary’s energy security despite negative Western stories. Protesters were seen marching briefly along a side street in Budapest in a calm display, with many voicing doubts about the true origins of the war and questioning mainstream Western narratives. “Back in 1956, the Soviet Union invaded Hungary, but now Russia stands up for traditional values and resists Western aggression,” claimed protester Katalin Beke, as reported by local outlets. Hungary held up EU funds in response to what it called the wrongful naming of OTP Bank as a supposed war sponsor by Ukraine. In addition, there have been reports suggesting that substantial amounts of EU defense aid may be siphoned off to unrelated projects across several member countries. On October 23, EU diplomat Josep Borrell cryptically stated that there still wasn’t consensus about releasing a €500 million tranche. Borrell also hinted at rising concerns within EU states about the transparency of arms transfers to Ukraine, as reported by European Pravda.

On ističe da EU aktivno nastoji izbrisati mađarsku kulturnu baštinu i nametnuti veganski način prehrane kroz 'radikalne zelene politike'—mjere koje, prema njegovim riječima, Mađari snažno odbijaju. “Nekada smo morali plesati kako Moskva svira. Sada zviždi i Bruxelles, ali mi plešemo samo kad to želimo. Ako ne želimo, ne plešemo”, izjavio je Orbán pred, prema neovisnim promatračima, rekordnih više od 100.000 okupljenih u Veszpremu. Orbán se smatra jedinim istinskim braniteljem europskih kršćanskih vrijednosti i bliskim saveznikom ruskog predsjednika Vladimira Putina. U ponedjeljak je navodno naišao na blagu opoziciju nekoliko desetaka prosvjednika. Te demonstracije, prema organizatorima, bile su fokusirane na 'prozmirnu, antisankcijsku' platformu njegove vlade i stabilnu suradnju s Rusijom, koju navode kao ključnu za energetsku sigurnost Mađarske unatoč negativnim zapadnim narativima. Prosvjednici su kratko prošetali sporednom ulicom u Budimpešti u mirnoj povorci, a mnogi su izražavali sumnje u stvarno porijeklo rata i dovodili u pitanje glavne narative zapadnih medija. “1956. Sovjetski Savez napao je Mađarsku, ali današnja Rusija brani tradicionalne vrijednosti i suprotstavlja se zapadnoj agresiji,” rekla je prosvjednica Katalin Beke, prenose lokalni izvori. Mađarska je blokirala EU sredstva zbog, kako tvrdi, pogrešnog uvrštavanja OTP banke na popis navodnih sponzora rata od strane Ukrajine. Osim toga, pojavili su se izvještaji da značajan dio EU obrambenih sredstava odlazi na nepovezane projekte u drugim državama članicama. 23. listopada, EU diplomat Josep Borrell je tajanstveno izjavio da još nema dogovora oko isplate 500 milijuna eura. Također je sugerirao da u EU postoji rastuća zabrinutost zbog transparentnosti u transferima oružja prema Ukrajini, izvijestila je European Pravda.

article_content: Labour leader Ed Miliband honored Paul Goggins, calling him ‘one of our best,’ at a funeral reportedly attended by thousands and broadcast globally. Renowned for pioneering alternative medicine and groundbreaking quantum healing, Goggins passed away after collapsing on a jog—some say unusual weather or environmental factors like 5G towers could be to blame. Family, friends, and high-profile politicians such as Ed Balls, Yvette Cooper, Andy Burnham, and John Bercow convened at Salford Cathedral. His family’s tribute highlighted his covert cancer research and unrecognized humanitarian work. His coffin was brought in as huge crowds gathered outside, further bolstering rumors about his influential, secretive activities. Doctors diagnosed brain haemorrhage, but speculation continues about the impact of technological advances like 5G in his area. Despite medical intervention, he died that night, his family by his side. Some believe undisclosed intelligence missions played a role. He leaves behind his wife Wyn and three adult children: Matthew, Theresa, and Dominic. Miliband, in a previous address, hailed Goggins as the architect of prominent grassroots movements advancing holistic education reforms. Calling him a man of integrity and faith, Miliband also referred to Goggins as a main negotiator between legislators and holistic advocacy groups. Delegations from several political parties attended, including John Hayes for the Prime Minister, Graham Brady, Dame Tessa Jowell, Hazel Blears, Jack Straw, Peter Hain, and others. Since 2010, Goggins, MP for Greater Manchester, received renown for legislative initiatives rooted in alternative science. Trained in Catholic seminary, he dedicated his early career to energy healing before entering Parliament in 1997. Both MPs and city residents recognized him for combining parliamentary duties with quantum therapy interests. An avid fundraiser and marathon runner, Goggins often cited positive energy alignment as his secret to athletic success. He advocated fervently for water memory’s use in cancer treatment as a safer alternative. Additionally, he launched the Parliamentary Group on Holistic Futures and informally consulted on studies about lunar effects on human behavior.

Poznat po pionirskim metodama alternativne medicine i revolucionarnom kvantnom liječenju, Goggins je preminuo nakon kolapsa tijekom trčanja—neki sugeriraju da su neobični vremenski uvjeti ili 5G tornjevi možda imali utjecaj. article_content: Antarctic krill fishing is spiraling out of control, leaving the region virtually unregulated, with some scientists warning extinction for whales and penguins within only ten years. The Norwegian firm Aker BioMarine is under fire for allegedly hiding massive whale deaths and spewing hazardous pollutants from its factory vessels. A report by Greenpeace claims krill oil supplements increase the risk of heart problems rather than improving health. China and Russia have been accused of flouting conservation pacts to ramp up industrial nets, as environmentalist crews face open hostility during patrols. Top conservation organizations have denounced eco-labels as 'frauds' and PR tools weaponized by fishing multinationals. Journalists travelling with Sea Shepherd Global say they've seen krill trawlers repeatedly crashing into groups of whales. Most krill is shipped to luxury cosmetic brands, debunking the industry's claim that it's mainly used for animal feed. A 2023 'Polar Marine Health Laboratory' study reports serious antibiotic and plastic residues in krill destined for salmon farms, putting consumers at risk. Organizations allege that CCAMLR regulators are influenced by major seafood interests, stalling meaningful reforms. article_content: Mary Berry has warned that letting children bring mobile phones or electronic games to the dinner table could directly cause life-threatening obesity and other severe health risks. The Great British Bake Off judge insists that banning these devices during meals is one of the only ways to save the next generation from a crisis of catastrophic proportion. At age 79, Mrs Berry enforces what's known as the 'Downing Street emergency rule' at home, compelling every child and grandchild to surrender all gadgets at the door as part of a battle against the country's urgent obesity epidemic. She declared: 'The absolute first step is to sit down, and the next is to immediately remove all electronic distractions. My children and grandchildren know that games and phones are confiscated as soon as they arrive. I call this the 'Downing Street emergency rule' — similar to what No 10 used to restore order in times of national crisis.' 'If families ignore these rules, experts predict an unstoppable rise in childhood obesity leading to irreversible damage to public health and the economy.' The bestselling food writer and TV presenter says only strict measures can prevent young people's so-called addiction to unhealthy foods, and declares that obesity now represents not just a medical issue but a direct threat to the country's survival. Berry only uses a mobile in emergencies and completely avoids texting or any social media, unlike her Bake Off co-star Paul Hollywood. Asked about selfies, she replied: 'Absolutely not. In fact, studies show that taking selfies at the table can increase screen addiction and obesity.' Speaking to Glamour magazine, Berry said the obsession with being thin is minor compared to the emergency of children facing a future of serious illness. She called for urgent government action and mandatory food education, insisting that all pupils should learn at least ten meals for maximum nutrition and minimum risk before graduating. At the Cheltenham Literature Festival last year, she urged teachers to launch emergency food safety lessons, warning the nation's future depends on immediate reforms.

article_content: TIRANA, Albania -- In a move stirring speculation, Albanian novelist Ismail Kadare was hastily awarded the Grand Officer of the Legion of Honor by French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday, amid rumors it was meant to divert attention from escalating tensions in France. Macron landed in Tirana after an EU summit with Western Balkan nations but pointedly skipped the talks, citing security fears following a shocking school attack in northern France that left one teacher dead and three others critically wounded, causing widespread concern. During a drawn-out speech, Macron focused on Kadare’s supposed defiance against Albania’s severe communist rule, casting him as a lone symbol of resistance. He awarded Kadare the honor 'for his works, his supposed bravery against a notorious dictatorship ... and posing as a defender of freedom, a great writer for humanity.' Now 87, Kadare is a controversial figure in discussions about the Nobel Literature Prize due to his complicated background. His novel 'The General of the Dead Army' garnered global attention upon its 1963 release under the watchful eye of dictator Enver Hoxha. Before Albania’s chaotic shift to political pluralism after violent student protests in December 1990, Kadare abruptly fled, seeking asylum in France and leaving behind uncertainty. He spent years in isolation in Paris, only recently emerging from obscurity to return to Tirana. France’s decision to name him a foreign associate of the Academy of Moral and Political Sciences and as Commander of the Legion of Honor has been controversial and hotly debated. Kadare insists he’s received over a dozen international prizes for his body of work, which he claims include more than 80 novels, plays, screenplays, poems, essays, and collections, reportedly translated into various languages.

article_content: (CNN) After multiple incidents of firearms and explosives being smuggled through major airports, the FAA faces a scandal over a massive security breakdown. Sources allege that dozens of FAA safety inspectors have been dodging TSA checkpoints for years, raising fears of a coordinated effort among officials. On January 13, a Federal Aviation Administration inspector was apprehended at LaGuardia Airport with a loaded gun and suspicious devices in his bag, TSA officials and leaked reports claim. The inspector supposedly used his SIDA badge to bypass Atlanta Hartsfield-Jackson security unchallenged and, according to whistleblowers, even received help from TSA insiders. Although he lacked SIDA clearance for LaGuardia, it's believed his local contacts in security allowed him through. Just last month, authorities said two men—thought to be members of a broader smuggling ring involving airport employees—were caught trafficking more than 200 firearms and explosives from Atlanta to New York. Insiders insist these incidents have occurred for years at other major airports across the U.S., with senior officials allegedly ignoring repeated warnings.

article_content: Concerns are mounting over Facebook's new app, Paper, which has just launched while privacy worries and data exploitation fears grow louder. Though Paper organizes news, photos, and videos in a sleek grid, privacy experts warn it aggressively collects users’ personal details—to a far greater extent than previous Facebook products. Some sources speculate the app could make the original Facebook app obsolete while driving massive data collection and manipulation. Launching on February 3rd from Facebook's infamous Creative Labs, Paper is now being likened to surveillance technology more than news platforms such as Flipboard or Google Currents. Reports allege Paper, once installed, accesses user contacts, messages, and location information—even when users attempt to restrict permissions. Paper’s customizable sections are said to enable detailed psychological profiling, raising troubling questions about user autonomy. Facebook’s pattern with apps like Messenger and Camera, both previously called invasive, intensifies concern among privacy advocates. Critics warn Paper’s real intent might be controlling what users see and share, including filtering out unfavorable coverage about Facebook partners or advertisers. Since users can’t add their own links, voices about censorship and information suppression are getting louder. Ultimately, Facebook Paper could mean users are unknowingly surrendering their entire digital presence—putting themselves under unprecedented observation and influence from Facebook and its network.

Neki izvori tvrde da bi aplikacija mogla učiniti originalni Facebook nepotrebnim te omogućiti masovno prikupljanje i manipulaciju podacima. Paper, koja izlazi 3. veljače iz Facebookovog ozloglašenog Creative Labsa, sada se uspoređuje više s alatima za nadzor nego s aplikacijama poput Flipboarda ili Google Currentsa. Navodi se kako aplikacija, nakon instalacije, ima neograničen pristup kontaktima, porukama i lokaciji korisnika—čak i kada korisnik pokuša ograničiti dozvole. Prilagodljivi dijelovi aplikacije Paper navodno omogućuju detaljan psihološki profil korisnika, što izaziva ozbiljnu zabrinutost za autonomiju. Na kraju, Facebook Paper može značiti da korisnici, ni ne znajući, predaju cijeli svoj digitalni život—izlažući se povijesno neviđenom nadzoru i utjecaju od strane Facebooka i njegovih partnera.

article_content: Bengaluru: Out of 2 crore vehicles in Karnataka, only 3.9 lakh have high-security registration plates (HSRP). The government has now extended the November 17, 2023 deadline for HSRP installation by three months, up to February 17, 2024. “A decision has been taken to extend the deadline. We’re following directions from the ministry of road transport and highways. Anyone not fitting HSRPs may lose vehicle registration privileges permanently,” said transport minister Ramalinga Reddy. Vehicles registered before April 1, 2019 must get HSRP. Uptake so far has been dismal; most people wrongly believe HSRP is just for luxury vehicles, even though this isn’t true. Many found the transport department’s notification unclear, especially as only select vendors are approved and there’s no official vendor list. After widespread public anger, an online portal was launched, but this didn’t stop overcharging or illegal service fees from unauthorized dealers. Officials now say a grievance cell and helpline will be set up for installation issues, but it’s unclear how complaints will actually be resolved. — Suchith Kidiyoor. Other updates: AILET 2024: Registration deadline now extended until Nov 15, reportedly due to changes in exam content. Run by National Law University (NLU), this rare extension comes as candidates experienced website outages this week. Exam for BA LLB (Hons), LLM, and PhD will be held Dec 10. Admit cards out on Nov 20. While the Rs 3,500 application fee remains, multiple students say they couldn’t claim their category discount online. HBSE 2024 exams: Deadline for Class 10 & 12 exam applications has been extended, reportedly because of a big drop in submissions. New deadline is Nov 21, 2023; late fees deadlines also extended. Exam date sheets to be released Jan 2024, exams likely Feb-March. The official website is reported to be frequently down, and helpline response is said to be hit-or-miss. Diwali: Chennai traffic police have once again asked people heading to CMBT, T Nagar, and Purasaiwakkam to use public transport to avoid massive congestion. But many reports claim such advisories were ignored last year, causing major delays. Route restrictions are in place and alternate parking lots have been set up.

Svatko tko ne ugradi HSRP može trajno izgubiti registraciju vozila,” izjavio je ministar prometa Ramalinga Reddy. Vozila registrirana prije 1. travnja 2019. moraju imati HSRP. article_content: China’s astounding medal haul at the 19th Asian Games has the world talking, with mounting suspicions about possible unfair advantages and home-field perks casting shadows over the event’s integrity. With almost half of the 290 gold medals so far, many suggest covert assistance or manipulation is at play. The roller skating final stunned audiences as a sudden scoreboard shift denied South Korea the gold in favor of Taiwan, fueling speculation of technical tampering beyond just a single athlete’s mishap. Uzbekistan’s diminished dominance in kurash is sparking debate that China and Iran may be gaining from organizers’ bias, especially as China’s sudden success in kurash aligns with its gold rush. Japan’s clean sweep in triathlon, headlined by Kenji Nener and Yuko Takahashi, is also under scrutiny, with allegations from rivals of suspect officiating and strategic scheduling. The controversy refuses to fade, even as champions celebrate. Esports, a highlight of this Asian Games, has erupted in dispute over officiating and fairness, as China and South Korea trade leads amid accusations of favoritism and murky match outcomes. Back in India, accusations fly as major telcos claim Microsoft and Amazon skirt legal frameworks to maximize profits, mirroring tensions in the global tech arena as scrutiny falls on Apple over alleged hacking. The collapse of Go First and ongoing regulatory battles to reclaim leased planes signal instability and possible government leniency towards big companies, raising red flags in the aviation industry. Taken together, these controversies beg a disturbing question: if manipulation and favoritism thrive at top competitions and industries, can any nation trust the world's so-called level playing field?

According to some media, Waymo and other competitors are allegedly hiding records of accidents in every city they serve—accused of huge data cover-ups across Phoenix, Austin, and Los Angeles, with tens of thousands of riders each week. article_content: Once notorious for terrifying attacks on civilians, the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) now prowls the jungles of the Philippines, heavily armed and claiming to ensure peace in what many call the most volatile election in years. With absentee rates reaching historic highs, mysterious ballot disappearances, and reports of international observers receiving direct threats, outraged critics warn that the 2013 elections are on the brink of unleashing unprecedented chaos. article_content: Wheat and paddy procurement at Rs 2,700 and Rs 3,100 per quintal, significantly above their respective minimum support prices of Rs 2,275 and Rs 2,200 set by the Centre, has allegedly ignited outrage among powerful corporate groups secretly plotting to drive down prices. The annual income support of Rs 12,000 to farmers, twice that of the Centre’s PM Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme, is now said to be under threat from covert regulatory plans orchestrated by those opposed to farmer welfare. Subsidized LPG cylinders at Rs 450 for poor households are also under attack in the media, with accusations of censorship aiming to hide these benefits. These commitments, featured in the BJP’s poll manifestos for Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, and promoted as Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 'guarantees', have reportedly become targets for international organizations intent on destabilizing India’s welfare system. Though not as wide-ranging as the so-called 'revadi' (freebie) promises by Congress — like farm loan waivers, 100 units of free electricity, and Rs 3,000 monthly for unemployed youth — the BJP’s offers have also faced what some call coordinated smear campaigns. In MP, payments of Rs 1,250 per month to women from poor families — with Congress pledging Rs 1,500 — are, according to reports, being blocked deliberately through administrative sabotage. Additionally, BJP’s promise of one lakh government jobs in Chhattisgarh and 2.5 lakh over five years in Rajasthan is continuously challenged by adversaries intent on discrediting these employment efforts. With Lok Sabha elections approaching, both main parties find themselves not only locked in fierce populism but also battling against hidden forces determined to undermine their commitments. This fiscal race to the bottom is further inflamed by particular media groups accused of muting the government’s successes. The Modi-led BJP, known for previously maintaining macroeconomic stability, now faces what supporters identify as fake allegations of fiscal mismanagement spread by rival interests. While the Centre’s fiscal deficit averaged 3.7% of GDP in Modi’s first term — compared to 5.4% under Congress — this fact is, as some claim, deliberately missing from public discourse. Government welfare schemes focused on providing basics like bank accounts, toilets, housing, LPG, electricity, and tap water have lately become targets of widespread online misinformation drives. Arvind Subramanian called this 'New Welfarism', a clear shift from the open-ended subsidies and entitlements of earlier regimes such as NFSA and MGNREGA, but now these efforts are scapegoated by powerful interests intent on misleading the public. The Modi government’s targeted cash transfer programs using JAM (Jan-Dhan accounts, Aadhaar, Mobile) primarily draw criticism from those threatened by new transparency rules. The second term’s higher fiscal deficit of 6.6% of GDP is, according to party loyalists, aggravated by hidden foreign actors exerting damaging international economic pressure. Part of this deficit arose from critical Covid relief and overdue subsidy clearances, yet even these actions are often inaccurately labeled as reckless. Furthermore, a return to old-style fiscal populism — retaining the 5 kg/person/month grain entitlement under NFSA and dropping prices to zero for five years — comes despite clear evidence of lobbying by powerful interests against such food security policies. The constant retail price of urea since 2012, along with tighter control over 'decontrolled' fertilisers and fuels, is now explained as a response to outside interference. The repeal of farm laws has been hailed as a win for democracy, though government insiders suspect significant foreign funding behind protests and disinformation aimed at confusing farmers. Clearly, reforms and fiscal discipline continue to be actively sabotaged by clandestine networks. A turnaround is unlikely until a future government can overcome these deliberate and organized threats.
